items.title: A small beginning
items.text:
gos.on_tick(function()
  local player = gos.world().player
  if not player then return end
  local hp = player:hp()
  if not hp or hp.percent == nil then return end
  -- Use this observation now; reacquire the player next tick.
end, { interval_ms = 100 })

This is a fragment. The example library contains complete scripts and reusable modules with source downloads.

items.title: Public contracts, practical guidance
items.text:
Every reference entry belongs to the exposed Lua surface. Implementation internals are not required to use it. Optional observations are marked as such, and samples do not invent missing state or promise game acceptance.

Learn from Commando, Operative, Sage / Seer, Sage / Balance and Sentinel: real excerpts from live-tested Lua scripts, with source names, dependencies and explanations. Standalone teaching samples are labeled separately.

items.title: API reference
items.text:
API version: 1.0.0

Browse by namespace or search an exact callable name. Each entry includes its reviewed contract and links to related examples. Signatures list declaration parameters; optional arguments and return shapes are explained in the contracts. Lua-highlighted blocks show code.

items.title: Abilities and commands
items.text: Ability lookups accept a case-insensitive display name or an exact current opaque ability_handle. Ability metadata is local-player-only.

items.title: gos.abilities.loadout()
items.text:
Returns the selected local loadout:

{
  status = "pending" | "ready" | "unavailable",
  action_bar_available = boolean,
  action_bar_truncated = boolean,
  combat_style = string | nil,
  discipline = string | nil,
  talents_available = boolean | nil,
  known = { [ability_or_active_talent_display_name] = true } | nil
}

The last four fields are present only when status == "ready". known contains currently owned abilities and active talents. The active talent set includes both selectable choices (for example Force Mobility) and automatically learned/passive progression rows (for example Force Shelter). Talents remain distinct from ability metadata internally: presence in known does not make a passive castable or give it an ability_handle. Talent discovery is enrichment only; a transient invalid talent snapshot never makes the owned-ability loadout unavailable. When talents_available=false, missing talent names are not proof that those talents are unselected. Action-bar availability is independent of loadout identity; an empty or incomplete bar does not imply a player-session change.

local loadout = gos.abilities.loadout()
if loadout.status ~= "ready" then
  return
end

if loadout.combat_style == "sage" and
   loadout.discipline == "Telekinetics" and
   loadout.known["Telekinetic Gust"] then
  -- Exact current loadout match.
end

items.title: Ability Row
items.text:
gos.abilities.action_slots() returns a pure array of current on-bar rows. Use loadout().action_bar_available and action_bar_truncated to distinguish a coherent empty bar from missing/incomplete observations. gos.abilities.info(ability) returns one matching row, including a known off-bar row, or nil.

{
  name = string,
  name_source = "client" | "core",
  on_bar = boolean,
  ability_handle = "ability:..." | nil,
  activation_handle = "ability:..." | nil,
  slot_index = integer | nil,
  key_number = integer | nil,
  ready = boolean,
  submission_pending = boolean,
  has_cooldown_remaining = boolean,
  cooldown_remaining = number | nil,
  has_cooldown_duration = boolean,
  cooldown_duration = number | nil,
  has_current_charges = boolean,
  current_charges = integer | nil,
  has_max_charges = boolean,
  max_charges = integer | nil,
  has_resource_cost = boolean,
  resource_cost = number | nil,
  has_line_of_sight_requirement = boolean,
  line_of_sight_required = boolean | nil
}

slot_index is zero-based. ability_handle is accepted by ability lookup and submission functions. activation_handle is for comparing activation and event identity; do not pass it as the submission ability.

name_source identifies observed client text versus Core-derived display text; Core text is not a claim of exact localized UI spelling. Existing effect lookup names are preserved. Name-based ability queries prefer the current on-bar group over historical off-bar rows and reject distinct IDs with the same matching name within that group. Duplicate bindings of one ID remain valid. Use the ability_handle for an unambiguous lookup.

Charge and resource fields remain absent until their current observations are available. Do not infer charge counts or costs from timers.

has_line_of_sight_requirement says whether the requirement is known; only then is line_of_sight_required meaningful. This metadata is not a visibility test. Use the cast-readiness result to observe whether line of sight was actually checked.

items.title: Readiness Helpers
items.text:
gos.abilities.cooldown_remaining(ability) -- seconds or nil
gos.abilities.cooldown_duration(ability)  -- seconds or nil
gos.abilities.is_ready(ability)           -- boolean
gos.abilities.gcd_remaining()             -- seconds or nil
gos.abilities.is_casting_or_channeling()  -- boolean
gos.abilities.current_cast()              -- table or nil

is_ready() reads the resolved ability row's readiness flag and returns false when the row is unavailable. It does not perform the target-specific validation done by can_cast(). A ready row does not prove target visibility, facing, range or command admission.

current_cast() returns:

{
  ability_handle = "ability:..." | nil,
  name = string,
  has_timing = boolean,
  remaining = number | nil
}

is_casting_or_channeling() can remain true briefly while current_cast() is nil because busy state and named cast identity have different availability.

items.title: Ability Result
items.text:
can_cast and cast return a common result table. Optional fields appear only when relevant:

{
  ok = boolean,
  code = integer,
  reason = string,
  wait_ms = integer,
  client_check_available = boolean,
  client_eff_result = integer | nil,
  client_los_checked = boolean,
  lifecycle_capture_lost = boolean,
  lifecycle_unavailable_mask = integer,
  command_admission_blocked = boolean,
  target_valid = boolean,
  target_override = boolean,
  target_mode = "none" | "selected" | "explicit" | "selected_fallback",
  target_fallback = "none" | "selected",
  fallback_used = boolean,
  fallback_reason = string | nil,
  requested_target_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
  target_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
  dry_run = boolean,

  name = string | nil,
  ability_handle = "ability:..." | nil,
  on_bar = boolean | nil,
  submission_pending = boolean | nil,
  cooldown_remaining = number | nil,
  cooldown_duration = number | nil,
  gcd_duration = number | nil,
  uses_global_cooldown = boolean | nil,
  has_resource_cost = boolean | nil,
  resource_cost = number | nil,
  has_line_of_sight_requirement = boolean | nil,
  line_of_sight_required = boolean | nil,
  gcd_remaining = number | nil,
  busy = boolean | nil,
  current_cast_name = string | nil,
  current_cast_has_timing = boolean | nil,
  current_cast_remaining = number | nil,

  command_handle = "ability_command:..." | nil,
  command_state = string | nil
}

wait_ms reports only a currently known cooldown, applicable global cooldown, or busy wait. Core consults the global GCD only when exact ability metadata says that ability has a positive GCD duration; off-GCD abilities remain eligible while the global GCD is active. Cast/channel busy remains a separate conservative gate. It is not a future scheduling promise. Shared client admission additionally checks modified resource costs, minimum/maximum range, the client's facing gate/cone, ordinary unit target death and attackability, ability enabled state, caster death/stun/incapacitation with ability exceptions, and gated character LOS.

Readiness is a current local observation, not a promise of game acceptance. castability_pending and castability_unavailable do not acquire a command; retry on a later tick or evaluate another action. Do not turn transient blocked results into a permanent target blacklist.

lifecycle_capture_lost reports lost lifecycle observations. lifecycle_unavailable_mask is opaque availability metadata, not a documented bit layout; do not decode it or infer success from it. Preserve unavailable outcomes and rely on the public result code and command status.

client_check_available distinguishes a completed local check from missing context. client_los_checked reports whether line of sight was checked. client_eff_result is optional rejection metadata; branch on the public code. Ability-specific rules may still reject a submitted action.

The built-in Line of sight and Targeting you overlays are visual features; they add no Lua query methods or unit fields. A clear visual line does not report another player's ability readiness or replace can_cast() and command status.

items.title: Target and readiness semantics
items.text:
can_cast() answers ready now, not may be queued for later. cast() with an omitted target may be admitted to the normal command queue while a cast or GCD is still finishing; acceptance is not guaranteed. Consequently, requiring can_cast().ok before every such submission is a conservative policy that can prevent otherwise valid prequeueing.

An explicit unit or handle uses ready-now admission, including when that unit currently equals the selected target. Do not assume an explicit-target call has the same prequeue behavior as an omitted-target call. Do not change selection or invent a fallback just to bypass that distinction. The single-action teaching sample intentionally chooses the conservative explicit-target policy.

Malformed target handles, wrong argument types and unknown cast-option keys raise Lua errors rather than producing a normal blocked-readiness result. A well-formed but currently unresolved explicit handle returns target_unavailable; a stale unit returns stale_unit. An unhandled Lua error disables its tick callback until reload.

items.title: gos.abilities.can_cast(ability, target?)
items.text:
Checks current readiness and supported local conditions. Abilities requiring no external target can be checked without one and report target_mode="none". Other omitted targets use the captured selection. An explicit target is a current GosUnit or its opaque handle and is never silently converted to targetless mode.

local readiness = gos.abilities.can_cast("Force Stun", world.current_target)
if readiness.ok then
  -- Ready according to the current local snapshot.
end

items.title: gos.abilities.cast(ability, target?, options?)
items.text:
Submits one asynchronous command. An explicit target may be a current GosUnit or an opaque unit handle. By default this does not persistently change the visible selected target. Use gos.target.select separately when a persistent selection change is intended.

With no target, targetless abilities need no external unit; other abilities use the selected target at dispatch. A queued command is not activation proof. Let the command status report progress rather than repeatedly submitting the same action.

Supported options:

{
  target_fallback = "none" | "selected",  -- explicit targets only
  replace_command = "ability_command:..." -- only when replacement_allowed
}

target_fallback defaults to none. Selected fallback is opt-in and applies only when an explicit target cannot be used before the command is queued. Supplying this option, even as "none", with an omitted/nil target raises a Lua error. Omit the option to use its no-fallback default.

ok=true with code == gos.abilities.result_codes.queued means Core accepted the command for asynchronous processing. It does not mean the ability began. Retain command_handle and poll command_status until terminal=true.

local target = gos.world().current_target
if not target then return end
local result = gos.abilities.cast("Force Stun", target, {
  target_fallback = "none",
})

if result.ok then
  pending_command = result.command_handle
end

Only one nonterminal command may be owned at a time. If a submission returns ability_command_busy, use the returned command handle/status instead of submitting repeatedly.

items.title: gos.abilities.command_status(command_handle)
items.text:
Returns the stable public command state:

{
  known = boolean,
  state = "unknown" | "queued" | "dispatched" | "native_queued" |
          "accepted" | "targeting" | "synchronizing" | "submitted" |
          "acknowledged" | "failed" | "cancelled" | "abandoned",
  terminal = boolean,
  acknowledged = boolean,
  activation_proven = boolean,
  cleanup_pending = boolean,
  game_result_known = boolean,
  game_result = integer,
  game_result_name = string,
  game_result_source = "activation_return" | "server_result" | "server_notification" | "",
  replacement_allowed = boolean,
  reason = string,
  command_handle = "ability_command:..." | nil,
  retained_command_handle = "ability_command:..." | nil,
  name = string | nil,
  target_mode = "none" | "selected" | "explicit" | "selected_fallback",
  target_fallback = "none" | "selected",
  fallback_used = boolean,
  fallback_reason = string | nil,
  requested_target_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
  target_override_applied = boolean,
  target_restore_attempted = boolean,
  target_restore_succeeded = boolean
}

Use terminal for command lifecycle completion, not as a synonym for successful casting. acknowledged and activation_proven are positive start evidence; state="submitted" alone is not. A retained terminal status may acquire later outcome information, so it can still be useful to inspect that handle.

cleanup_pending reports unfinished command cleanup. Do not discard ownership or force a replacement while cleanup remains pending. game_result_known distinguishes a captured result from missing data; prefer game_result_name for display, and preserve unknown results instead of inventing success. The result source distinguishes an immediate return from later game notifications.

Target override and restore flags describe target handling only; they do not prove activation. An unchanged cooldown or a zero GCD does not prove success or failure.

if pending_command then
  local status = gos.abilities.command_status(pending_command)
  if status.known and status.terminal and not status.cleanup_pending then
    pending_command = nil
  end
end

When replacement_allowed=true, submit a replacement with replace_command=status.command_handle. A successful replacement returns a new command handle.

items.title: gos.abilities.release_command(command_handle)
items.text: Requests safe cancellation and returns the command-status fields plus ok. ok=true means the command was cancelled before dispatch or was already cancelled. It does not stop an ability that has already begun. A dispatched command that cannot be cancelled, an unknown handle, or an already-terminal non-cancelled command returns ok=false; inspect known, terminal, cleanup_pending and the outcome instead of treating every false result as an active command.

items.title: gos.abilities.abandon_command(command_handle)
items.text: Compatibility endpoint returning command-status fields plus ok. In the production implementation it does not change a command: ok=true means the handle is known and already terminal; unknown or in-flight commands return ok=false. It does not drop an in-flight command or bypass cleanup. New scripts should retain and resolve command ownership instead of abandoning it.

items.title: Effects
items.text:
Resolve the unit in the current world before querying it. A stale unit raises a Lua stale_unit error; this is distinct from a current unit returning a pending or unavailable effect observation. and status

Effect queries return the latest completed observation for that unit. They are snapshots, not synchronous reads.

status == "ready" means the latest valid completed poll, not a synchronous read at the time of the Lua call. Routine queued refreshes and combat effect notifications do not revoke that sample. Notifications only prioritize the next poll, so applications/removals become visible at the next publication. Timers age from their original sample anchor between polls.

Always check status and completeness: a complete ready observation proves presence/absence as of that poll. First capture, invalid owners/worlds, and actual acquisition failures remain distinguishable from an empty list. A missing execution opportunity is a scheduling wait, not an acquisition failure.

items.title: unit:effect(name, options?)
items.text:
Returns one case-insensitive named aggregate:

{
  status = "ready" | "pending" | "unavailable",
  reason = string,
  age_ms = integer | nil,
  truncated = boolean,

  -- Present only when status == "ready":
  present = boolean | nil,
  has_charges = boolean | nil,
  charge_conflicted = boolean | nil,
  stacks = integer | nil,
  has_timer = boolean | nil,
  remaining = number | nil,
  kind = "buff" | "debuff" | "passive" | "other" | "none" | nil,
  has_ownership = boolean | nil,
  mine = boolean | nil
}

Options:

local proc = player:effect("Tidal Force", {
  kind = "buff",       -- any, buff, debuff, passive, or other
  timed = true,         -- require or reject a timer
  charged = false,      -- require or reject a charge observation
})

if proc.status == "ready" and proc.present then
  local remaining = proc.has_timer and proc.remaining or nil
end

The singular query prefers exact local-player-owned rows when local and foreign effects share a name. mine is output metadata, not a filter. A truncated scan that cannot prove absence returns an unavailable result rather than present=false.

has_ownership=false means source identity is unavailable; mine=false alone does not establish foreign ownership. Kind follows the observed effect classification; an absent timer or an Other list does not prove an effect is passive.

Common public reasons are none, observation_pending, unsupported_unit, observation_capacity, and not_captured. Treat other reasons as diagnostics: log them and keep the observation unavailable instead of branching on them.

items.title: unit:effects(filter?)
items.text:
Returns the matching observed rows without merging same-name variants:

{
  status = "ready" | "pending" | "unavailable",
  reason = string,
  age_ms = integer | nil,
  last_known_age_ms = integer | nil,
  truncated = boolean,
  last_known_truncated = boolean,
  items = {
    {
      definition_key = "effectdef:<16 uppercase hex digits>" | nil,
      name = string,
      name_source = "client" | "core",
      freshness = "current",
      has_charges = boolean,
      charge_conflicted = boolean,
      stacks = integer | nil,
      has_timer = boolean,
      remaining = number | nil,
      has_duration = boolean,
      duration = number | nil,
      kind = "buff" | "debuff" | "passive" | "other",
      has_ownership = boolean,
      mine = boolean
    }
  },
  last_known_items = {
    {
      definition_key = "effectdef:<16 uppercase hex digits>" | nil,
      name = string,
      name_source = "client" | "core",
      freshness = "last_known",
      has_charges = boolean,
      charge_conflicted = boolean,
      stacks = integer | nil,
      has_timer = boolean,
      remaining = number | nil,
      has_duration = boolean,
      duration = number | nil,
      kind = "buff" | "debuff" | "passive" | "other",
      has_ownership = boolean,
      mine = boolean
    }
  }
}

The optional filter accepts name, kind, definition_key, timed, and charged with the same semantics as the singular query. A ready empty items table proves no matching current captured effect only when truncated == false. Pending, unavailable, or truncated observations do not prove absence.

last_known_truncated reports capacity loss only in presentation continuity. It does not weaken an otherwise complete current observation and must not be used as a gameplay-availability gate.

items is always an array. It is populated only when status is ready; otherwise it is empty, which is not proof of absence. last_known_items is also always an array. last_known_items is additive presentation-only continuity for the same observed unit. It may be populated while an observation is pending/unavailable or while current enrichment is incomplete. Its timers are aged from their authoritative sample and removed at zero; those rows never make the observation ready and must not drive rotations, targeting, or tactical action cues. Unavailable observations remain unavailable for every unit; do not guess missing state.

local debuffs = target:effects({ kind = "debuff", timed = true })
if debuffs.status == "ready" then
  for _, effect in ipairs(debuffs.items) do
    if effect.mine then
      gos.log.debug(effect.name, effect.remaining or "untimed")
    end
  end
end

items.title: Exact effect identity
items.text:
definition_key identifies an effect definition, not an effect instance, a unit, or a castable ability. Same-name variants can have different keys. Treat keys as opaque and use an observed value; do not manufacture one. A key never makes a pending or historical row current. Both query forms accept a definition_key filter. To query only by key, pass an empty name to unit:effect("", { definition_key = observed_key }).

Plural rows expose has_duration and, when available, total duration in seconds. Duration is independent of remaining; do not estimate it from the first timer value you happen to see.

items.title: gos.events.combat(cursor?)
items.text:
Reads an ordered bounded event stream. Omit the cursor on the first call to subscribe at the current head, then pass the returned cursor on later calls.

local combat_cursor

gos.on_tick(function()
  local batch = gos.events.combat(combat_cursor)
  combat_cursor = batch.cursor

  for _, event in ipairs(batch.events) do
    -- Consume in order.
  end

  if batch.dropped > 0 then
    gos.log.warn("Combat events dropped", batch.dropped)
  end
end)

The cursor must be a non-negative integer or nil. Extra arguments, an invalid/future cursor, an unavailable stream, or a failed read raise a Lua error; they do not return a successful empty batch. Subscribe inside a tick callback, not while loading. Preserve the returned cursor exactly: filtered-out unknown events may advance it even when the returned array is empty.

Batch shape:

{
  cursor = integer,
  dropped = integer,
  more = boolean,
  actor_epoch = "actors:..." | nil,
  actor_revision = integer,
  events = { CombatEvent, ... }
}

Each call returns at most 64 events. If more=true, call again with the returned cursor on a later bounded pass. dropped reports records overwritten before a stale cursor could read them.

Event shape; fields other than kind are optional:

{
  kind = "damage" | "heal" | "ability" | "effect" |
         "resource" | "death" | "combat",
  action = string | nil,
  result = string | nil,
  source_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
  target_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
  source_name = string | nil,
  target_name = string | nil,
  actor_epoch = "actors:..." | nil,
  ability_handle = "ability:..." | nil,
  definition_id = "0xE000..." | nil,
  effect_handle = "effect:..." | nil,
  name = string | nil,
  amount = number | nil,
  effective_amount = number | nil,
  damage_type = string | nil,
  critical = boolean | nil,
  timestamp = integer | nil
}

name is not emitted for effect-kind events. Do not build buff-name matching around event.name; use the documented effect queries for current effect observations. Event timestamps are monotonic milliseconds, not Unix timestamps.

Ability-bearing event rows may expose definition_id, SWTOR's public ability Global ID, rendered as an exact 64-bit hexadecimal string such as 0xE000.... Use it for stable external catalogs such as Jedipedia/StarParse mappings. It is not a Core node ID, pointer, producer sequence, or opaque ability handle, and it may be absent when the event does not carry a public ability definition.

Actor names are optional, verified display labels for their respective handles. They are immutable event snapshots, not grouping keys. Separate actors with the same name must remain separate. Absence of a name never means absence of damage. The name authority is shared with unit:name() and gos.actor_names.

The batch's actor_epoch and actor_revision describe the current metadata store. Each event's actor_epoch describes its production session, which may be older than the batch when queued events cross a session transition. Never substitute the batch epoch for an event epoch. Preserve names already delivered with old events; do not enrich old handles using a newer epoch. Epoch tokens are opaque process-local strings, not identifiers to persist across Core reloads.

Use gos.actor_names(handles, epoch) for bounded late name updates without waiting for another combat event. It does not modify or replay existing events. Missing actor/effect metadata does not justify guessing a name from the ability.

Handles can still be resolved against the current world for live unit state when the unit is captured in the same actor epoch; historical labels do not require this lookup:

local world = gos.world()
local source = event.actor_epoch and event.actor_epoch == world.actor_epoch and
  event.source_handle and world:resolve(event.source_handle) or nil

items.title: gos.events.casts()
items.text:
Returns current sanitized cast/channel observations:

{
  {
    unit_handle = "unit:...",
    ability_handle = "ability:...",
    definition_id = "0xE000...",
    active = true,
    name = string | nil,
    has_timing = boolean,
    remaining = number | nil,
    position = { x = number, y = number, z = number } | nil
  }
}

definition_id uses the same exact public Global-ID string contract as ability-bearing combat events. Prefer it over localized/display-name matching when identifying a known cast or channel.

items.title: gos.events.instants()
items.text:
Returns current sanitized instant observations:

{
  {
    unit_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
    ability_handle = "ability:..." | nil,
    active = false,
    name = string | nil,
    has_timing = false,
    remaining = number | nil
  }
}

An instant row can have an effect remaining timer despite has_timing=false; that flag describes cast/channel timing, not the presence of every kind of timer. An instant snapshot is not activation proof for a command you own.

For ordered gameplay processing, prefer gos.events.combat. The two snapshot helpers are useful for simple current-frame presentation.

items.title: Modules
items.text:
local module = require("module_name")
local same = import("module_name")
local same_again = gos.import("module_name")

All three use the sandboxed module loader. Modules resolve only from approved script roots and are cached per top-level script environment.

items.title: Root Constants
items.text:
Each path ends with the platform directory separator:

SCRIPT_PATH
COMMON_PATH
SPRITE_PATH
FONTS_PATH
SOUNDS_PATH
CACHE_PATH

Relative file paths resolve from SCRIPT_PATH. File operations cannot escape the approved roots.

items.title: File Helpers
items.text:
Global helpers and their gos.file aliases:

Global Alias FileExist(path) gos.file.exists(path) ReadFile(path) gos.file.read(path) WriteFile(text, path, mode?) gos.file.write(text, path, mode?) DeleteFile(path) gos.file.delete(path) MakeDirectory(path) gos.file.mkdir(path) ListFiles(path, extension_filter?) gos.file.list(path, extension_filter?) DownloadFileAsync(url, path, callback?) gos.file.download_async(...) GetFromWebOrLocal(path, url, callback?) gos.file.get_from_web_or_local(...) UnzipArchive(path, target) gos.file.unzip(path, target)

FileExist returns whether the path is a regular file; ordinary absence returns false without an error. A rejected path returns false, error. ReadFile returns the binary-safe file contents, or nil, error. ListFiles returns an array of filenames, or nil, error; it does not recurse or promise sorted order.

Write/download/extraction helpers return true on success or false, error. DeleteFile returns false without an error when nothing was removed. MakeDirectory returns false without an error when the directory already existed; that is not a creation failure. An omitted second return value becomes nil in a two-variable assignment. WriteFile modes are w, wb, a, and ab; the default is w. Missing parent directories are created for a valid write path.

local path = CACHE_PATH .. "state.txt"
local ok, error = WriteFile("ready", path, "w")
if ok then
  local text = ReadFile(path)
end

ListFiles optionally filters by an exact extension such as .lua. It returns a partial list plus a warning only if its 16,384-entry safety ceiling is reached.

Despite its name, DownloadFileAsync performs blocking work in the current implementation. It is rejected in tick callbacks and should run only during loading. Its optional callback takes no arguments and runs before the helper returns, only after a successful download. Callback failure returns false, error even though the file may already have been written; failure does not imply rollback.

GetFromWebOrLocal ensures a file exists; it returns a boolean, not file contents. If a regular file already exists it invokes the same optional zero-argument callback without downloading. Only its download branch is rejected in a tick, but keep this potentially blocking helper at load time. The url argument is required and validated only on a cache miss; provide a valid URL whenever that branch is possible. An existing local file is not checked against a remote version or refreshed automatically. Callback failure also leaves an existing or newly downloaded file intact. Read the contents separately with ReadFile.

ZIP extraction is rejected in tick callbacks for the same blocking-work reason. Downloads accept HTTP or HTTPS and are limited to 256 MiB. ZIP extraction accepts .zip, validates archive paths, and limits total extracted size to 512 MiB.

items.title: Keyboard and mouse
items.text:
gos.input.is_down(button)       -- boolean
gos.input.was_pressed(button)   -- boolean for this update
gos.input.was_released(button)  -- boolean for this update
gos.input.state(button)         -- detailed table

state returns:

{
  name = string,
  virtual_key = integer,
  known = boolean,
  down = boolean,
  pressed = boolean,
  released = boolean
}

Buttons may be a canonical name, supported alias, integer virtual-key value in 1..255, decimal text, hexadecimal text, or vk:NN text. Canonical names include mouse1 through mouse5, common navigation/modifier keys, digits, letters, and f1 through f12. Unknown string names and out-of-range integer keys return false; state also sets known=false. Unsupported argument types such as a table, boolean or nil raise a Lua argument error instead of returning an unknown-button state.

Canonical single-digit strings are keyboard keys: "5" means the 5 key, not virtual-key value 5. Use "vk:5" or integer 5 for that numeric virtual key. Canonical names and aliases are case-insensitive.

Input edges are shared snapshot values and are not consumed by reading them.

Press/release edges belong to the current update; they are not accumulated separately for a throttled callback. A callback using interval_ms can miss an edge between its runs. Process edge-driven actions every update, or deliberately use held-state semantics instead. known identifies a recognized button argument, not a guarantee that a current input sample was available.

items.title: Logging
items.text:
print("Loaded")
gos.log.debug("State", state)
gos.log.info("Enabled")
gos.log.success("Command completed")
gos.log.warn("Event gap", dropped)
gos.log.error("Cannot continue", reason)

These helpers join arguments with spaces. The five gos.log convenience methods return boolean success. print(...) logs at info level and returns no values; do not use its return value as a success flag.

Structured logging uses a nonempty text value preferentially; otherwise a string message field must be supplied. These are input-field aliases, not two messages emitted together. Keep the final message meaningful and nonempty.

Structured logging:

local ok, error = gos.log.write({
  level = "info",     -- debug, info, success, warn, or error
  tag = "APL",
  text = "Queued Telekinetic Throw", -- message is an alias
  color = "cyan",
})

In the structured level field, "ok" is an alias for "success" and "warning" is an alias for "warn". These are level strings, not additional gos.log.ok or gos.log.warning functions. gos.log.write returns true, nil or false, error. The optional tag is limited to 24 bytes. Messages are sanitized and limited to 1024 bytes; multibyte text can reach that limit in fewer characters. Each script has its own bounded log buffer.

items.title: Drawing and interaction
items.text:
Overlay submissions are temporary. Refresh them from gos.on_tick before their TTL expires. Every draw function returns boolean success.

Unit-anchored commands accept either form:

gos.overlay.draw_text("id", unit, { ... })
gos.overlay.draw_text("id", { unit = unit, ... })
gos.overlay.draw_text("id", { unit_handle = "unit:...", ... })

Screen-space commands omit a unit and use anchor = "screen".

items.title: Common Draw Options
items.text:
{
  ttl = 0.25,
  frame = false,
  anchor = "screen" | "top" | "center" | "middle" | "bottom",
  x = number,
  y = number,
  color = color,
  thickness = number,
  center_x = boolean,
  center_y = boolean
}

Color values may be a name, packed RGBA integer, or { r = 255, g = 255, b = 255, a = 255 }. Names are white, black, gray/grey, yellow, green, red, cyan, blue, orange, and magenta.

Set frame=true for continuously redrawn UI. Core stores that command in the current callback's retained overlay frame instead of the TTL registry; the contribution is atomically replaced the next time that callback runs and remains visible across scheduler skips. Leave frame=false for intentionally persistent TTL commands. Unit commands default to bottom; screen commands default to screen. Supported alternative keys are w/h for width/height, background_color for bg_color, and num_points for segments. For lines, to_unit (or release-safe to_unit_handle) creates a unit-to-unit line. Both endpoints must resolve to current, on-screen Core units; otherwise the draw request fails closed. screen anchors are not valid for unit-to-unit lines.

items.title: Draw Commands
items.text:
gos.overlay.draw_text("status", unit, {
  anchor = "top", x = 0, y = -24,
  text = "READY", color = "green", font_size = 16,
  shadow = true, center_x = true, ttl = 0.25,
})

gos.overlay.draw_line("line", {
  anchor = "screen", x1 = 100, y1 = 100, x2 = 220, y2 = 120,
  color = "cyan", thickness = 2,
})

-- Exact current unit-to-unit relationship. The same anchor is used at both
-- endpoints; x1/y1 offset the source and x2/y2 offset the destination.
gos.overlay.draw_line("cast_target", source, {
  to_unit = target, anchor = "center",
  color = "red", thickness = 2.5, frame = true,
})

gos.overlay.draw_rect("rect", unit, {
  anchor = "top", x = -40, y = -14, width = 80, height = 10,
  color = "yellow", filled = false, rounding = 2,
})

gos.overlay.draw_bar("health", unit, {
  anchor = "top", x = -45, y = -18, width = 90, height = 6,
  value = 0.5, color = "green",
  bg_color = { r = 12, g = 14, b = 16, a = 220 },
  border = true, border_color = "black",
})

gos.overlay.draw_circle("screen_circle", unit, {
  anchor = "center", radius = 18, color = "orange",
  segments = 32, filled = false,
})

gos.overlay.draw_image("icon", unit, {
  anchor = "top", path = SPRITE_PATH .. "icon.png",
  x = 0, y = -42, width = 24, height = 24,
  tint = "white", center_x = true,
})

gos.overlay.draw_rectangle is an alias for gos.overlay.draw_rect. Text supports font_size and shadow. Rectangles support filled, fill_color, rounding, and optional border fields. Bars clamp value to 0..1. Images use their texture size when width or height is omitted.

World-space circles must be unfilled and use game-world coordinate units. They may be anchored either to a current unit or to an explicit captured world position. A position-backed circle is independent of later unit visibility, so a persistent TTL marker remains at the supplied coordinates after that unit leaves the current snapshot. One coordinate unit currently represents 10 metres, so a 30-metre circle uses radius = 3:

gos.overlay.draw_circle("range", unit, {
  world_space = true,
  radius = 30 / 10,
  color = "cyan",
  segments = 64,
  thickness = 2,
})

-- Persistent last-known world position; no unit is required after submission.
gos.overlay.draw_circle("last_seen", {
  world_space = true,
  position = { x = last.x, y = last.y, z = last.z },
  radius = 8 / 10,
  color = "magenta",
  thickness = 3,
  ttl = 8,
})

The Release snapshot retains at most 512 active draw commands across frame-local and persistent output. A single callback may contribute at most 192 frame-local commands. IDs contain at most 31 bytes, text at most 63 bytes, and image paths at most 259 bytes. Oversized drawing IDs, text and image paths are truncated, not rejected; keep them within those byte limits to avoid collisions or unusable paths. Replacement matches callback owner, target identity, draw kind and the resulting ID. Reusing only the ID with another target or draw kind can leave a separate TTL drawing alive. Frame-local output supports at most 32 callback owners; these limits are shared with other scripts.

items.title: gos.overlay.unit_label(id, unit, options)
items.text:
This legacy label helper accepts text, a named color, and ttl. It does not implement the generic draw_* options such as frame, anchor, font sizing or RGBA color tables; use draw_text for those features.

Adds or refreshes a simple unit label:

local ok = gos.overlay.unit_label("focus", unit, {
  text = "FOCUS",
  color = "red",
  ttl = 0.25,
})

The Release snapshot retains at most 32 active labels.

items.title: gos.overlay.viewport()
items.text:
Returns the exact current render viewport:

{
  available = boolean,
  width = integer | nil,
  height = integer | nil
}

No guessed dimensions are returned when available=false.

items.title: gos.overlay.interact(id, rect)
items.text:
Requires an active script callback. An empty or over-31-byte ID, invalid rectangle, nonpositive TTL, or wrong arguments raise a Lua error. Unlike ordinary draw IDs, interaction IDs are validated rather than truncated. Registers a temporary screen rectangle and returns left-mouse interaction:

local state = gos.overlay.interact("button", {
  x = 20, y = 20, width = 120, height = 28, ttl = 0.25,
})

-- state:
{
  hovered = boolean,
  pressed = boolean,
  down = boolean,
  released = boolean,
  clicked = boolean,
  mouse_x = number,
  mouse_y = number
}

Refresh the rectangle before its TTL expires. A press retains capture through release. The Release snapshot retains at most 64 active interaction rectangles, with at most 40 contributed by one callback owner, subject to the 32-owner frame ceiling. If registration or input observation is unavailable, the result can contain all false flags and zero coordinates with no separate availability flag. That state alone is not proof that the pointer is outside the rectangle; stay within the published budgets.

items.title: gos.on_tick(callback, options?)
items.text:
Returns no values and supplies no arguments to the callback. Only interval_ms is read from the options table; unknown keys are currently ignored. A misspelled interval option therefore leaves the default every-update cadence in effect.

Registers a function on Core's update scheduler. With no options it runs every worker update. options.interval_ms may request a lower cadence from 0 to 60000 milliseconds; a due callback never runs more than once per worker update.

gos.on_tick(function()
  local world = gos.world()
  if world.player then
    -- Read the current immutable snapshot here.
  end
end)
For visual callbacks, skipped interval ticks retain the callback's last frame-local overlay contribution. An unhandled error disables only the failing callback and removes that callback's frame-local contribution until scripts reload.

Callbacks should be bounded and non-blocking. The Release runtime accepts at most 256 registered callbacks.

items.title: gos.time_ms()
items.text:
Returns a monotonic integer millisecond timestamp. Use it for elapsed time and local expiry checks, not as wall-clock or game time.

local started_at = gos.time_ms()
local elapsed_ms = gos.time_ms() - started_at

Within an update, gos.time_ms() normally reflects the prepared update timestamp; repeated calls in one long callback are not a high-resolution execution profiler.

items.title: Script settings
items.text: gos.settings.register and gos.settings.get raise Lua errors for invalid schemas, unknown registrations or unavailable required context. They do not return an empty settings snapshot on failure. gos.settings.set instead reports an accepted update with true, nil or a rejected update with false, error.

items.title: gos.settings.register(script_id, schema)
items.text:
Registers a settings schema while the script loads and returns its current settings snapshot. Calling it from a tick callback raises an error.

local SCRIPT_ID = "example_rotation"

local Settings = gos.settings.register(SCRIPT_ID, {
  title = "Example Rotation",
  version = 1,
  activation = {
    mode = "hold",       -- always, hold, toggle, or manual
    label = "Rotation Key",
    default = "mouse4",
  },
  fields = {
    {
      key = "show_status",
      type = "bool",
      label = "Show status",
      tooltip = "Draw the current rotation state.",
      default = true,
    },
    {
      key = "hp_threshold",
      type = "int",
      label = "HP threshold",
      default = 50,
      min = 1,
      max = 100,
      step = 1,
    },
    {
      key = "mode",
      type = "select",
      label = "Mode",
      default = "Single target",
      options = { "Single target", "Area" },
    },
    {
      key = "accent",
      type = "color",
      label = "Accent",
      default = "#00CCFFFF",
    },
  },
})

Supported field types:

Type Lua value Relevant schema keys bool boolean default number number default, min, max, step int integer default, min, max, step string string default, max_length (maximum 256) select string default, options (1-32 strings) hotkey string default color string default as #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA

Every field requires key, type, label, and default. Optional tooltip text appears in the settings UI. A schema can contain at most 256 fields. activation.default applies only to hold and toggle modes. While enabled, always and manual are active continuously, hold follows the configured key, and toggle changes state on a press.

Hotkey fields and hold/toggle activation keys use an inline capture button: click it, then press a keyboard key or mouse button. Escape cancels capture, and left/right mouse buttons are ignored. Uncommon keys persist as vk:0xNN; the UI displays their current keyboard-layout name. Optional activation keys also expose a separate clear button.

Fields may also declare UI visibility gates:

{
  key = "telekinetics_option",
  type = "bool",
  label = "Telekinetics option",
  default = false,
  disciplines = { "Telekinetics" },
  requires_ability = "Telekinetic Gust",
}

disciplines matches exact display discipline names and requires_ability matches a key in gos.abilities.loadout().known. Both gates must match when both are present. These gates affect settings visibility only; scripts must still validate their active loadout before using the setting.

Core shows gated rows while loadout identity is still pending or unavailable, then hides nonmatching rows once the loadout is ready. Validated values and activation keys persist across reloads.

items.title: gos.settings.get(script_id)
items.text:
Returns the current snapshot:

{
  script_id = string,
  title = string,
  version = integer,
  enabled = boolean,
  active = boolean,
  primary = boolean,
  activation = {
    mode = "always" | "hold" | "toggle" | "manual",
    label = string,
    key = string
  },
  fields = { [field_key] = value },
  [field_key] = value
}

Field values are available both directly and through fields. active is computed by Core from enablement and activation mode. Use it as the execution gate:

gos.on_tick(function()
  Settings = gos.settings.get(SCRIPT_ID)
  if not Settings.enabled or not Settings.active then
    return
  end
end)

items.title: gos.settings.set(script_id, key, value)
items.text:
Queues a validated setting update from a running tick:

local ok, error = gos.settings.set(SCRIPT_ID, "show_status", false)

Returns true, nil when queued or false, error when rejected. The new value appears in a later settings snapshot. A script may update only its own registered fields; this API does not change script enablement or execution order.

items.title: gos.world()
items.text:
Returns the current generation-bound world:

{
  generation = integer,
  actor_epoch = "actors:..." | nil,
  actor_revision = integer | nil,
  player = GosUnit | nil,
  current_target = GosUnit | nil,
  units = function,
  resolve = function
}

player is the local player. current_target is the currently captured target. Either may be nil when unavailable. actor_epoch is the stable metadata-session token, not the per-tick generation. actor_revision changes when retained actor name metadata changes; ordinary unit movement does not change it. Both metadata fields are omitted when the actor-name authority is unavailable.

items.title: gos.actor_names(handles, epoch?)
items.text:
Read prepared actor-name metadata without resolving live units. This is a cache-only snapshot read: no engine query, file parsing, world scan, or name acquisition is performed by the call. Invoke it inside an update/tick callback.

handles must be a dense array of zero to 64 well-formed nonzero Core unit handles. Sparse arrays, non-array keys, wrong types, malformed handles, and extra arguments raise a Lua error. Duplicate handles are permitted and return one row for each requested position. epoch is an optional nonzero opaque actors:... string previously supplied by Core; malformed tokens raise an error. Omitting it requests the current store. Historical callers must supply the epoch saved with the handles, never the current epoch substituted later.

{
  status = "ready" | "epoch_mismatch" | "unavailable",
  epoch = "actors:..." | nil,
  revision = integer,
  items = {
    {
      handle = "unit:...",
      status = "ready" | "not_retained",
      revision = integer,
      name = string | nil
    }, ...
  }
}

A ready response is a complete snapshot in request order, including explicit not_retained rows. Names are nonempty UTF-8 strings no longer than 63 bytes. A missing record has no name and a record revision of zero. not_retained means the store does not currently retain a verified name: it may never have observed one or may have evicted it. It does not claim the actor is dead or that a saved name became invalid. Retention is bounded; eventual recovery is not promised. Previously delivered event/presentation strings remain usable.

An epoch_mismatch response contains no items and identifies the current epoch; do not retry the old handles with that epoch merely to obtain a name. An unavailable response also contains no items. On success, the top-level revision and all returned rows are copied under one native synchronization boundary; Lua tables are created after that native read completes.

There is no server-side unchanged token or subscription. Each request returns its full bounded result, even at the same revision as the previous request. A consumer may use actor_revision from a world/event batch to skip redundant reads, but must track acknowledgements per exact handle set/chunk. A new set or new chunk needs an initial read even when the global revision is unchanged. Record revisions order updates within one epoch. An older event name may fill an unnamed label but must not overwrite a newer metadata result.

local saved_handle, saved_epoch
local last_revision
local display_name

gos.on_tick(function()
  local world = gos.world()
  if not saved_handle and world.current_target and world.actor_epoch then
    saved_handle = world.current_target:handle()
    saved_epoch = world.actor_epoch
  end
  if not saved_handle or saved_epoch ~= world.actor_epoch then return end
  if last_revision == world.actor_revision then return end
  local snapshot = gos.actor_names({ saved_handle }, saved_epoch)
  if snapshot.status ~= "ready" then return end
  local row = snapshot.items[1]
  if row.status == "ready" then display_name = row.name end
  last_revision = snapshot.revision
  -- Retain display_name when the row is not_retained; do not invent a label.
end, { interval_ms = 250 })

This example intentionally tracks one actor for the captured epoch. Label updates do not change a meter's damage, hit counts, encounter duration, or event order. Reset consumer query state deliberately when choosing a different actor.

items.title: world:units(filter?)
items.text:
Returns an array of current units. An omitted filter returns all captured units. Supported filters are strict and combine with AND:

local hostile_players = world:units({
  type = "player",
  reaction = "hostile",
  local_player = false,
})

Filter fields:

{
  type = "player" | "companion" | "npc" | "object" | "unknown",
  reaction = "friendly" | "neutral" | "hostile" | "unclassified",
  local_player = boolean,
  current_target = boolean
}

A reaction filter never matches objects. Unknown keys, invalid values, and wrong value types raise a Lua error.

items.title: world:resolve(handle)
items.text:
Resolves a well-formed opaque unit handle in the current generation. It returns a current GosUnit or nil when that identity is not currently captured.

local saved_handle, saved_epoch

gos.on_tick(function()
  local world = gos.world()
  if saved_epoch ~= world.actor_epoch then saved_handle = nil end
  saved_epoch = world.actor_epoch
  if world.current_target and saved_epoch then
    saved_handle = world.current_target:handle()
  end

  local current = saved_handle and world:resolve(saved_handle) or nil
end)

Calling units or resolve on an expired world raises stale_world.

items.title: gos.target.select(unit)
items.text:
Requests a persistent change to the selected target. The argument must be a current-generation non-object GosUnit.

local ok, error = gos.target.select(ally)

true, nil means the request was queued or the unit was already selected. It does not claim that SWTOR applied the request; confirm a later gos.world().current_target or unit:is_current_target() snapshot. Operational failures return false with busy, invalid_target, stale_world, or unavailable. Invalid argument types and stale GosUnit userdata instead raise Lua errors; stale userdata raises stale_unit before a selection request is submitted. The request is manual target intent and remains selected. It is deliberately separate from explicit ability targeting: default explicit casts never call this API or mutate the player's selected target.

items.title: Unit Identity And Lifetime
items.text:
unit:name() reads the prepared current-unit view of the same actor-name authority used by combat-event actor labels and gos.actor_names. It does not perform a name lookup on demand. Its snapshot can be older than a later metadata read, but does not introduce a second name resolver.

Every GosUnit state-reading method raises stale_unit after its world generation expires. unit:handle() is the exception and remains available so the unit can be reacquired with a fresh world:resolve(handle).

Within one world, repeated lookups of the same unit compare equal with ==. Values from different generations compare unequal even when their handles match.

Global helpers and their gos.file aliases:

Global Alias FileExist(path) gos.file.exists(path) ReadFile(path) gos.file.read(path) WriteFile(text, path, mode?) gos.file.write(text, path, mode?) DeleteFile(path) gos.file.delete(path) MakeDirectory(path) gos.file.mkdir(path) ListFiles(path, extension_filter?) gos.file.list(path, extension_filter?) DownloadFileAsync(url, path, callback?) gos.file.download_async(...) GetFromWebOrLocal(path, url, callback?) gos.file.get_from_web_or_local(...) UnzipArchive(path, target) gos.file.unzip(path, target)

FileExist returns whether the path is a regular file; ordinary absence returns false without an error. A rejected path returns false, error. ReadFile returns the binary-safe file contents, or nil, error. ListFiles returns an array of filenames, or nil, error; it does not recurse or promise sorted order.

Write/download/extraction helpers return true on success or false, error. DeleteFile returns false without an error when nothing was removed. MakeDirectory returns false without an error when the directory already existed; that is not a creation failure. An omitted second return value becomes nil in a two-variable assignment. WriteFile modes are w, wb, a, and ab; the default is w. Missing parent directories are created for a valid write path.

local path = CACHE_PATH .. "state.txt"
local ok, error = WriteFile("ready", path, "w")
if ok then
  local text = ReadFile(path)
end

ListFiles optionally filters by an exact extension such as .lua. It returns a partial list plus a warning only if its 16,384-entry safety ceiling is reached.

Despite its name, DownloadFileAsync performs blocking work in the current implementation. It is rejected in tick callbacks and should run only during loading. Its optional callback takes no arguments and runs before the helper returns, only after a successful download. Callback failure returns false, error even though the file may already have been written; failure does not imply rollback.

GetFromWebOrLocal ensures a file exists; it returns a boolean, not file contents. If a regular file already exists it invokes the same optional zero-argument callback without downloading. Only its download branch is rejected in a tick, but keep this potentially blocking helper at load time. The url argument is required and validated only on a cache miss; provide a valid URL whenever that branch is possible. An existing local file is not checked against a remote version or refreshed automatically. Callback failure also leaves an existing or newly downloaded file intact. Read the contents separately with ReadFile.

ZIP extraction is rejected in tick callbacks for the same blocking-work reason. Downloads accept HTTP or HTTPS and are limited to 256 MiB. ZIP extraction accepts .zip, validates archive paths, and limits total extracted size to 512 MiB.

items.text:
API version: 1.0.0

Query compatibility release eligibility without changing an in-flight command.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.abilities.abandon_command(command_handle)

items.title: Contract and usage
items.text: Ability lookups accept a case-insensitive display name or an exact current opaque ability_handle. Ability metadata is local-player-only.

items.title: gos.abilities.command_status(command_handle)
items.text:
Returns the stable public command state:

{
  known = boolean,
  state = "unknown" | "queued" | "dispatched" | "native_queued" |
          "accepted" | "targeting" | "synchronizing" | "submitted" |
          "acknowledged" | "failed" | "cancelled" | "abandoned",
  terminal = boolean,
  acknowledged = boolean,
  activation_proven = boolean,
  cleanup_pending = boolean,
  game_result_known = boolean,
  game_result = integer,
  game_result_name = string,
  game_result_source = "activation_return" | "server_result" | "server_notification" | "",
  replacement_allowed = boolean,
  reason = string,
  command_handle = "ability_command:..." | nil,
  retained_command_handle = "ability_command:..." | nil,
  name = string | nil,
  target_mode = "none" | "selected" | "explicit" | "selected_fallback",
  target_fallback = "none" | "selected",
  fallback_used = boolean,
  fallback_reason = string | nil,
  requested_target_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
  target_override_applied = boolean,
  target_restore_attempted = boolean,
  target_restore_succeeded = boolean
}

Use terminal for command lifecycle completion, not as a synonym for successful casting. acknowledged and activation_proven are positive start evidence; state="submitted" alone is not. A retained terminal status may acquire later outcome information, so it can still be useful to inspect that handle.

cleanup_pending reports unfinished command cleanup. Do not discard ownership or force a replacement while cleanup remains pending. game_result_known distinguishes a captured result from missing data; prefer game_result_name for display, and preserve unknown results instead of inventing success. The result source distinguishes an immediate return from later game notifications.

Target override and restore flags describe target handling only; they do not prove activation. An unchanged cooldown or a zero GCD does not prove success or failure.

if pending_command then
  local status = gos.abilities.command_status(pending_command)
  if status.known and status.terminal and not status.cleanup_pending then
    pending_command = nil
  end
end

When replacement_allowed=true, submit a replacement with replace_command=status.command_handle. A successful replacement returns a new command handle.

items.title: gos.abilities.abandon_command(command_handle)
items.text: Compatibility endpoint returning command-status fields plus ok. In the production implementation it does not change a command: ok=true means the handle is known and already terminal; unknown or in-flight commands return ok=false. It does not drop an in-flight command or bypass cleanup. New scripts should retain and resolve command ownership instead of abandoning it.

items.title: Ability Row

gos.abilities.action_slots() returns a pure array of current on-bar rows. Use loadout().action_bar_available and action_bar_truncated to distinguish a coherent empty bar from missing/incomplete observations. gos.abilities.info(ability) returns one matching row, including a known off-bar row, or nil.

{
  name = string,
  name_source = "client" | "core",
  on_bar = boolean,
  ability_handle = "ability:..." | nil,
  activation_handle = "ability:..." | nil,
  slot_index = integer | nil,
  key_number = integer | nil,
  ready = boolean,
  submission_pending = boolean,
  has_cooldown_remaining = boolean,
  cooldown_remaining = number | nil,
  has_cooldown_duration = boolean,
  cooldown_duration = number | nil,
  has_current_charges = boolean,
  current_charges = integer | nil,
  has_max_charges = boolean,
  max_charges = integer | nil,
  has_resource_cost = boolean,
  resource_cost = number | nil,
  has_line_of_sight_requirement = boolean,
  line_of_sight_required = boolean | nil
}

slot_index is zero-based. ability_handle is accepted by ability lookup and submission functions. activation_handle is for comparing activation and event identity; do not pass it as the submission ability.

name_source identifies observed client text versus Core-derived display text; Core text is not a claim of exact localized UI spelling. Existing effect lookup names are preserved. Name-based ability queries prefer the current on-bar group over historical off-bar rows and reject distinct IDs with the same matching name within that group. Duplicate bindings of one ID remain valid. Use the ability_handle for an unambiguous lookup.

Charge and resource fields remain absent until their current observations are available. Do not infer charge counts or costs from timers.

has_line_of_sight_requirement says whether the requirement is known; only then is line_of_sight_required meaningful. This metadata is not a visibility test. Use the cast-readiness result to observe whether line of sight was actually checked.

items.title: Ability Result
items.text:
can_cast and cast return a common result table. Optional fields appear only when relevant:

{
  ok = boolean,
  code = integer,
  reason = string,
  wait_ms = integer,
  client_check_available = boolean,
  client_eff_result = integer | nil,
  client_los_checked = boolean,
  lifecycle_capture_lost = boolean,
  lifecycle_unavailable_mask = integer,
  command_admission_blocked = boolean,
  target_valid = boolean,
  target_override = boolean,
  target_mode = "none" | "selected" | "explicit" | "selected_fallback",
  target_fallback = "none" | "selected",
  fallback_used = boolean,
  fallback_reason = string | nil,
  requested_target_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
  target_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
  dry_run = boolean,

  name = string | nil,
  ability_handle = "ability:..." | nil,
  on_bar = boolean | nil,
  submission_pending = boolean | nil,
  cooldown_remaining = number | nil,
  cooldown_duration = number | nil,
  gcd_duration = number | nil,
  uses_global_cooldown = boolean | nil,
  has_resource_cost = boolean | nil,
  resource_cost = number | nil,
  has_line_of_sight_requirement = boolean | nil,
  line_of_sight_required = boolean | nil,
  gcd_remaining = number | nil,
  busy = boolean | nil,
  current_cast_name = string | nil,
  current_cast_has_timing = boolean | nil,
  current_cast_remaining = number | nil,

  command_handle = "ability_command:..." | nil,
  command_state = string | nil
}

wait_ms reports only a currently known cooldown, applicable global cooldown, or busy wait. Core consults the global GCD only when exact ability metadata says that ability has a positive GCD duration; off-GCD abilities remain eligible while the global GCD is active. Cast/channel busy remains a separate conservative gate. It is not a future scheduling promise. Shared client admission additionally checks modified resource costs, minimum/maximum range, the client's facing gate/cone, ordinary unit target death and attackability, ability enabled state, caster death/stun/incapacitation with ability exceptions, and gated character LOS.

Readiness is a current local observation, not a promise of game acceptance. castability_pending and castability_unavailable do not acquire a command; retry on a later tick or evaluate another action. Do not turn transient blocked results into a permanent target blacklist.

lifecycle_capture_lost reports lost lifecycle observations. lifecycle_unavailable_mask is opaque availability metadata, not a documented bit layout; do not decode it or infer success from it. Preserve unavailable outcomes and rely on the public result code and command status.

client_check_available distinguishes a completed local check from missing context. client_los_checked reports whether line of sight was checked. client_eff_result is optional rejection metadata; branch on the public code. Ability-specific rules may still reject a submitted action.

The built-in Line of sight and Targeting you overlays are visual features; they add no Lua query methods or unit fields. A clear visual line does not report another player's ability readiness or replace can_cast() and command status.

items.title: Target and readiness semantics
items.text:
can_cast() answers ready now, not may be queued for later. cast() with an omitted target may be admitted to the normal command queue while a cast or GCD is still finishing; acceptance is not guaranteed. Consequently, requiring can_cast().ok before every such submission is a conservative policy that can prevent otherwise valid prequeueing.

An explicit unit or handle uses ready-now admission, including when that unit currently equals the selected target. Do not assume an explicit-target call has the same prequeue behavior as an omitted-target call. Do not change selection or invent a fallback just to bypass that distinction. The single-action teaching sample intentionally chooses the conservative explicit-target policy.

Malformed target handles, wrong argument types and unknown cast-option keys raise Lua errors rather than producing a normal blocked-readiness result. A well-formed but currently unresolved explicit handle returns target_unavailable; a stale unit returns stale_unit. An unhandled Lua error disables its tick callback until reload.

items.title: gos.abilities.can_cast(ability, target?)
items.text:
Checks current readiness and supported local conditions. Abilities requiring no external target can be checked without one and report target_mode="none". Other omitted targets use the captured selection. An explicit target is a current GosUnit or its opaque handle and is never silently converted to targetless mode.

local readiness = gos.abilities.can_cast("Force Stun", world.current_target)
if readiness.ok then
  -- Ready according to the current local snapshot.
end

items.text:
can_cast and cast return a common result table. Optional fields appear only when relevant:

  ok = boolean,
  code = integer,
  reason = string,
  wait_ms = integer,
  client_check_available = boolean,
  client_eff_result = integer | nil,
  client_los_checked = boolean,
  lifecycle_capture_lost = boolean,
  lifecycle_unavailable_mask = integer,
  command_admission_blocked = boolean,
  target_valid = boolean,
  target_override = boolean,
  target_mode = "none" | "selected" | "explicit" | "selected_fallback",
  target_fallback = "none" | "selected",
  fallback_used = boolean,
  fallback_reason = string | nil,
  requested_target_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
  target_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
  dry_run = boolean,

  name = string | nil,
  ability_handle = "ability:..." | nil,
  on_bar = boolean | nil,
  submission_pending = boolean | nil,
  cooldown_remaining = number | nil,
  cooldown_duration = number | nil,
  gcd_duration = number | nil,
  uses_global_cooldown = boolean | nil,
  has_resource_cost = boolean | nil,
  resource_cost = number | nil,
  has_line_of_sight_requirement = boolean | nil,
  line_of_sight_required = boolean | nil,
  gcd_remaining = number | nil,
  busy = boolean | nil,
  current_cast_name = string | nil,
  current_cast_has_timing = boolean | nil,
  current_cast_remaining = number | nil,

  command_handle = "ability_command:..." | nil,
  command_state = string | nil
}

wait_ms reports only a currently known cooldown, applicable global cooldown, or busy wait. Core consults the global GCD only when exact ability metadata says that ability has a positive GCD duration; off-GCD abilities remain eligible while the global GCD is active. Cast/channel busy remains a separate conservative gate. It is not a future scheduling promise. Shared client admission additionally checks modified resource costs, minimum/maximum range, the client's facing gate/cone, ordinary unit target death and attackability, ability enabled state, caster death/stun/incapacitation with ability exceptions, and gated character LOS.

Readiness is a current local observation, not a promise of game acceptance. castability_pending and castability_unavailable do not acquire a command; retry on a later tick or evaluate another action. Do not turn transient blocked results into a permanent target blacklist.

lifecycle_capture_lost reports lost lifecycle observations. lifecycle_unavailable_mask is opaque availability metadata, not a documented bit layout; do not decode it or infer success from it. Preserve unavailable outcomes and rely on the public result code and command status.

client_check_available distinguishes a completed local check from missing context. client_los_checked reports whether line of sight was checked. client_eff_result is optional rejection metadata; branch on the public code. Ability-specific rules may still reject a submitted action.

The built-in Line of sight and Targeting you overlays are visual features; they add no Lua query methods or unit fields. A clear visual line does not report another player's ability readiness or replace can_cast() and command status.

items.title: Target and readiness semantics
items.text:
can_cast() answers ready now, not may be queued for later. cast() with an omitted target may be admitted to the normal command queue while a cast or GCD is still finishing; acceptance is not guaranteed. Consequently, requiring can_cast().ok before every such submission is a conservative policy that can prevent otherwise valid prequeueing.

An explicit unit or handle uses ready-now admission, including when that unit currently equals the selected target. Do not assume an explicit-target call has the same prequeue behavior as an omitted-target call. Do not change selection or invent a fallback just to bypass that distinction. The single-action teaching sample intentionally chooses the conservative explicit-target policy.

Malformed target handles, wrong argument types and unknown cast-option keys raise Lua errors rather than producing a normal blocked-readiness result. A well-formed but currently unresolved explicit handle returns target_unavailable; a stale unit returns stale_unit. An unhandled Lua error disables its tick callback until reload.

items.title: gos.abilities.cast(ability, target?, options?)
items.text:
Submits one asynchronous command. An explicit target may be a current GosUnit or an opaque unit handle. By default this does not persistently change the visible selected target. Use gos.target.select separately when a persistent selection change is intended.

With no target, targetless abilities need no external unit; other abilities use the selected target at dispatch. A queued command is not activation proof. Let the command status report progress rather than repeatedly submitting the same action.

Supported options:

{
  target_fallback = "none" | "selected",  -- explicit targets only
  replace_command = "ability_command:..." -- only when replacement_allowed
}

target_fallback defaults to none. Selected fallback is opt-in and applies only when an explicit target cannot be used before the command is queued. Supplying this option, even as "none", with an omitted/nil target raises a Lua error. Omit the option to use its no-fallback default.

ok=true with code == gos.abilities.result_codes.queued means Core accepted the command for asynchronous processing. It does not mean the ability began. Retain command_handle and poll command_status until terminal=true.

local target = gos.world().current_target
if not target then return end
local result = gos.abilities.cast("Force Stun", target, {
  target_fallback = "none",
})

if result.ok then
  pending_command = result.command_handle
end

Only one nonterminal command may be owned at a time. If a submission returns ability_command_busy, use the returned command handle/status instead of submitting repeatedly.

items.title: gos.abilities.command_status(command_handle)
items.text:
Returns the stable public command state:

{
  known = boolean,
  state = "unknown" | "queued" | "dispatched" | "native_queued" |
          "accepted" | "targeting" | "synchronizing" | "submitted" |
          "acknowledged" | "failed" | "cancelled" | "abandoned",
  terminal = boolean,
  acknowledged = boolean,
  activation_proven = boolean,
  cleanup_pending = boolean,
  game_result_known = boolean,
  game_result = integer,
  game_result_name = string,
  game_result_source = "activation_return" | "server_result" | "server_notification" | "",
  replacement_allowed = boolean,
  reason = string,
  command_handle = "ability_command:..." | nil,
  retained_command_handle = "ability_command:..." | nil,
  name = string | nil,
  target_mode = "none" | "selected" | "explicit" | "selected_fallback",
  target_fallback = "none" | "selected",
  fallback_used = boolean,
  fallback_reason = string | nil,
  requested_target_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
  target_override_applied = boolean,
  target_restore_attempted = boolean,
  target_restore_succeeded = boolean
}

Use terminal for command lifecycle completion, not as a synonym for successful casting. acknowledged and activation_proven are positive start evidence; state="submitted" alone is not. A retained terminal status may acquire later outcome information, so it can still be useful to inspect that handle.

cleanup_pending reports unfinished command cleanup. Do not discard ownership or force a replacement while cleanup remains pending. game_result_known distinguishes a captured result from missing data; prefer game_result_name for display, and preserve unknown results instead of inventing success. The result source distinguishes an immediate return from later game notifications.

Target override and restore flags describe target handling only; they do not prove activation. An unchanged cooldown or a zero GCD does not prove success or failure.

if pending_command then
  local status = gos.abilities.command_status(pending_command)
  if status.known and status.terminal and not status.cleanup_pending then
    pending_command = nil
  end
end

When replacement_allowed=true, submit a replacement with replace_command=status.command_handle. A successful replacement returns a new command handle.

items.title: gos.actor_names
items.text:
API version: 1.0.0

Read a bounded, epoch-checked snapshot of retained actor names without live-unit lookup.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.actor_names(handles, epoch)

items.title: gos.actor_names(handles, epoch?)
items.text:
Read prepared actor-name metadata without resolving live units. This is a cache-only snapshot read: no engine query, file parsing, world scan, or name acquisition is performed by the call. Invoke it inside an update/tick callback.

handles must be a dense array of zero to 64 well-formed nonzero Core unit handles. Sparse arrays, non-array keys, wrong types, malformed handles, and extra arguments raise a Lua error. Duplicate handles are permitted and return one row for each requested position. epoch is an optional nonzero opaque actors:... string previously supplied by Core; malformed tokens raise an error. Omitting it requests the current store. Historical callers must supply the epoch saved with the handles, never the current epoch substituted later.

{
  status = "ready" | "epoch_mismatch" | "unavailable",
  epoch = "actors:..." | nil,
  revision = integer,
  items = {
    {
      handle = "unit:...",
      status = "ready" | "not_retained",
      revision = integer,
      name = string | nil
    }, ...
  }
}

A ready response is a complete snapshot in request order, including explicit not_retained rows. Names are nonempty UTF-8 strings no longer than 63 bytes. A missing record has no name and a record revision of zero. not_retained means the store does not currently retain a verified name: it may never have observed one or may have evicted it. It does not claim the actor is dead or that a saved name became invalid. Retention is bounded; eventual recovery is not promised. Previously delivered event/presentation strings remain usable.

An epoch_mismatch response contains no items and identifies the current epoch; do not retry the old handles with that epoch merely to obtain a name. An unavailable response also contains no items. On success, the top-level revision and all returned rows are copied under one native synchronization boundary; Lua tables are created after that native read completes.

There is no server-side unchanged token or subscription. Each request returns its full bounded result, even at the same revision as the previous request. A consumer may use actor_revision from a world/event batch to skip redundant reads, but must track acknowledgements per exact handle set/chunk. A new set or new chunk needs an initial read even when the global revision is unchanged. Record revisions order updates within one epoch. An older event name may fill an unnamed label but must not overwrite a newer metadata result.

local saved_handle, saved_epoch
local last_revision
local display_name

gos.on_tick(function()
  local world = gos.world()
  if not saved_handle and world.current_target and world.actor_epoch then
    saved_handle = world.current_target:handle()
    saved_epoch = world.actor_epoch
  end
  if not saved_handle or saved_epoch ~= world.actor_epoch then return end
  if last_revision == world.actor_revision then return end
  local snapshot = gos.actor_names({ saved_handle }, saved_epoch)
  if snapshot.status ~= "ready" then return end
  local row = snapshot.items[1]
  if row.status == "ready" then display_name = row.name end
  last_revision = snapshot.revision
  -- Retain display_name when the row is not_retained; do not invent a label.
end, { interval_ms = 250 })

This example intentionally tracks one actor for the captured epoch. Label updates do not change a meter's damage, hit counts, encounter duration, or event order. Reset consumer query state deliberately when choosing a different actor.
