items.title: gos.events.combat
items.text:
API version: 1.0.0

Consume ordered combat events using a retained cursor, with loss and backlog reporting.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.events.combat(cursor)

items.title: gos.events.combat(cursor?)
items.text:
Reads an ordered bounded event stream. Omit the cursor on the first call to subscribe at the current head, then pass the returned cursor on later calls.

local combat_cursor

gos.on_tick(function()
  local batch = gos.events.combat(combat_cursor)
  combat_cursor = batch.cursor

  for _, event in ipairs(batch.events) do
    -- Consume in order.
  end

  if batch.dropped > 0 then
    gos.log.warn("Combat events dropped", batch.dropped)
  end
end)

The cursor must be a non-negative integer or nil. Extra arguments, an invalid/future cursor, an unavailable stream, or a failed read raise a Lua error; they do not return a successful empty batch. Subscribe inside a tick callback, not while loading. Preserve the returned cursor exactly: filtered-out unknown events may advance it even when the returned array is empty.

Batch shape:

{
  cursor = integer,
  dropped = integer,
  more = boolean,
  actor_epoch = "actors:..." | nil,
  actor_revision = integer,
  events = { CombatEvent, ... }
}

Each call returns at most 64 events. If more=true, call again with the returned cursor on a later bounded pass. dropped reports records overwritten before a stale cursor could read them.

Event shape; fields other than kind are optional:

{
  kind = "damage" | "heal" | "ability" | "effect" |
         "resource" | "death" | "combat",
  action = string | nil,
  result = string | nil,
  source_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
  target_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
  source_name = string | nil,
  target_name = string | nil,
  actor_epoch = "actors:..." | nil,
  ability_handle = "ability:..." | nil,
  definition_id = "0xE000..." | nil,
  effect_handle = "effect:..." | nil,
  name = string | nil,
  amount = number | nil,
  effective_amount = number | nil,
  damage_type = string | nil,
  critical = boolean | nil,
  timestamp = integer | nil
}

name is not emitted for effect-kind events. Do not build buff-name matching around event.name; use the documented effect queries for current effect observations. Event timestamps are monotonic milliseconds, not Unix timestamps.

Ability-bearing event rows may expose definition_id, SWTOR's public ability Global ID, rendered as an exact 64-bit hexadecimal string such as 0xE000.... Use it for stable external catalogs such as Jedipedia/StarParse mappings. It is not a Core node ID, pointer, producer sequence, or opaque ability handle, and it may be absent when the event does not carry a public ability definition.

Actor names are optional, verified display labels for their respective handles. They are immutable event snapshots, not grouping keys. Separate actors with the same name must remain separate. Absence of a name never means absence of damage. The name authority is shared with unit:name() and gos.actor_names.

The batch's actor_epoch and actor_revision describe the current metadata store. Each event's actor_epoch describes its production session, which may be older than the batch when queued events cross a session transition. Never substitute the batch epoch for an event epoch. Preserve names already delivered with old events; do not enrich old handles using a newer epoch. Epoch tokens are opaque process-local strings, not identifiers to persist across Core reloads.

Use gos.actor_names(handles, epoch) for bounded late name updates without waiting for another combat event. It does not modify or replay existing events. Missing actor/effect metadata does not justify guessing a name from the ability.

Handles can still be resolved against the current world for live unit state when the unit is captured in the same actor epoch; historical labels do not require this lookup:

local world = gos.world()
local source = event.actor_epoch and event.actor_epoch == world.actor_epoch and
  event.source_handle and world:resolve(event.source_handle) or nil

items.text:
Global helpers and their gos.file aliases:

Global Alias FileExist(path) gos.file.exists(path) ReadFile(path) gos.file.read(path) WriteFile(text, path, mode?) gos.file.write(text, path, mode?) DeleteFile(path) gos.file.delete(path) MakeDirectory(path) gos.file.mkdir(path) ListFiles(path, extension_filter?) gos.file.list(path, extension_filter?) UnzipArchive(path, target) gos.file.unzip(path, target)

FileExist returns whether the path is a regular file; ordinary absence returns false without an error. A rejected path returns false, error. ReadFile returns the binary-safe file contents, or nil, error. ListFiles returns an array of filenames, or nil, error; it does not recurse or promise sorted order.

Write/download/extraction helpers return true on success or false, error. DeleteFile returns false without an error when nothing was removed. MakeDirectory returns false without an error when the directory already existed; that is not a creation failure. An omitted second return value becomes nil in a two-variable assignment. WriteFile modes are w, wb, a, and ab; the default is w. Missing parent directories are created for a valid write path.

local ok, error = WriteFile("ready", path, "w")
if ok then
  local text = ReadFile(path)
end

ListFiles optionally filters by an exact extension such as .lua. It returns a partial list plus a warning only if its 16,384-entry safety ceiling is reached.

Despite its name, DownloadFileAsync performs blocking work in the current implementation. It is rejected in tick callbacks and should run only during loading. Its optional callback takes no arguments and runs before the helper returns, only after a successful download. Callback failure returns false, error even though the file may already have been written; failure does not imply rollback.

GetFromWebOrLocal ensures a file exists; it returns a boolean, not file contents. If a regular file already exists it invokes the same optional zero-argument callback without downloading. Only its download branch is rejected in a tick, but keep this potentially blocking helper at load time. The url argument is required and validated only on a cache miss; provide a valid URL whenever that branch is possible. An existing local file is not checked against a remote version or refreshed automatically. Callback failure also leaves an existing or newly downloaded file intact. Read the contents separately with ReadFile.

ZIP extraction is rejected in tick callbacks for the same blocking-work reason. Downloads accept HTTP or HTTPS and are limited to 256 MiB. ZIP extraction accepts .zip, validates archive paths, and limits total extracted size to 512 MiB.

items.title: gos.input.is_down
items.text:
API version: 1.0.0

Read whether a supported keyboard or mouse button is held.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.input.is_down(button)

items.title: Contract and usage
items.text:
gos.input.is_down(button)       -- boolean
gos.input.was_pressed(button)   -- boolean for this update
gos.input.was_released(button)  -- boolean for this update
gos.input.state(button)         -- detailed table

state returns:

{
  name = string,
  virtual_key = integer,
  known = boolean,
  down = boolean,
  pressed = boolean,
  released = boolean
}

Buttons may be a canonical name, supported alias, integer virtual-key value in 1..255, decimal text, hexadecimal text, or vk:NN text. Canonical names include mouse1 through mouse5, common navigation/modifier keys, digits, letters, and f1 through f12. Unknown string names and out-of-range integer keys return false; state also sets known=false. Unsupported argument types such as a table, boolean or nil raise a Lua argument error instead of returning an unknown-button state.

Canonical single-digit strings are keyboard keys: "5" means the 5 key, not virtual-key value 5. Use "vk:5" or integer 5 for that numeric virtual key. Canonical names and aliases are case-insensitive.

Input edges are shared snapshot values and are not consumed by reading them.

Press/release edges belong to the current update; they are not accumulated separately for a throttled callback. A callback using interval_ms can miss an edge between its runs. Process edge-driven actions every update, or deliberately use held-state semantics instead. known identifies a recognized button argument, not a guarantee that a current input sample was available.

items.title: gos.log.debug
items.text:
API version: 1.0.0

Write to the script log; rate-limit repeated messages and omit personal data.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.log.debug(...)

items.title: Contract and usage
items.text:
print("Loaded")
gos.log.debug("State", state)
gos.log.info("Enabled")
gos.log.success("Command completed")
gos.log.warn("Event gap", dropped)
gos.log.error("Cannot continue", reason)

These helpers join arguments with spaces. The five gos.log convenience methods return boolean success. print(...) logs at info level and returns no values; do not use its return value as a success flag.

Structured logging uses a nonempty text value preferentially; otherwise a string message field must be supplied. These are input-field aliases, not two messages emitted together. Keep the final message meaningful and nonempty.

Structured logging:

local ok, error = gos.log.write({
  level = "info",     -- debug, info, success, warn, or error
  tag = "APL",
  text = "Queued Telekinetic Throw", -- message is an alias
  color = "cyan",
})

In the structured level field, "ok" is an alias for "success" and "warning" is an alias for "warn". These are level strings, not additional gos.log.ok or gos.log.warning functions. gos.log.write returns true, nil or false, error. The optional tag is limited to 24 bytes. Messages are sanitized and limited to 1024 bytes; multibyte text can reach that limit in fewer characters. Each script has its own bounded log buffer.

items.title: gos.on_tick(callback, options?)
items.text:
Returns no values and supplies no arguments to the callback. Only interval_ms is read from the options table; unknown keys are currently ignored. A misspelled interval option therefore leaves the default every-update cadence in effect.

Registers a function on Core's update scheduler. With no options it runs every worker update. options.interval_ms may request a lower cadence from 0 to 60000 milliseconds; a due callback never runs more than once per worker update.

gos.on_tick(function()
  local world = gos.world()
  if world.player then
    -- Read the current immutable snapshot here.
  end
end)
For visual callbacks, skipped interval ticks retain the callback's last frame-local overlay contribution. An unhandled error disables only the failing callback and removes that callback's frame-local contribution until scripts reload.

Callbacks should be bounded and non-blocking. The Release runtime accepts at most 256 registered callbacks.

{
  ttl = 0.25,
  frame = false,
  anchor = "screen" | "top" | "center" | "middle" | "bottom",
  x = number,
  y = number,
  color = color,
  thickness = number,
  center_x = boolean,
  center_y = boolean
}

  shadow = true, center_x = true, ttl = 0.25,
})

gos.overlay.draw_line("line", {
  anchor = "screen", x1 = 100, y1 = 100, x2 = 220, y2 = 120,
  color = "cyan", thickness = 2,
})

-- endpoints; x1/y1 offset the source and x2/y2 offset the destination.

  to_unit = target, anchor = "center",
  color = "red", thickness = 2.5, frame = true,

  anchor = "top", x = -40, y = -14, width = 80, height = 10,
  color = "yellow", filled = false, rounding = 2,
})

  anchor = "top", x = -45, y = -18, width = 90, height = 6,
  value = 0.5, color = "green",
  bg_color = { r = 12, g = 14, b = 16, a = 220 },
  border = true, border_color = "black",
})

  anchor = "center", radius = 18, color = "orange",
  segments = 32, filled = false,
})

gos.overlay.draw_image("icon", unit, {
  anchor = "top", path = SPRITE_PATH .. "icon.png",
  x = 0, y = -42, width = 24, height = 24,
  tint = "white", center_x = true,

  color = "cyan",
  segments = 64,
  thickness = 2,

Overlay submissions are temporary. Refresh them from gos.on_tick before their TTL expires. Every draw function returns boolean success.

Unit-anchored commands accept either form:

gos.overlay.draw_text("id", unit, { ... })
gos.overlay.draw_text("id", { unit = unit, ... })
gos.overlay.draw_text("id", { unit_handle = "unit:...", ... })

Screen-space commands omit a unit and use anchor = "screen".

items.title: Common Draw Options
items.text:
{
  ttl = 0.25,
  frame = false,
  anchor = "screen" | "top" | "center" | "middle" | "bottom",
  x = number,
  y = number,
  color = color,
  thickness = number,
  center_x = boolean,
  center_y = boolean
}

Color values may be a name, packed RGBA integer, or { r = 255, g = 255, b = 255, a = 255 }. Names are white, black, gray/grey, yellow, green, red, cyan, blue, orange, and magenta.

Set frame=true for continuously redrawn UI. Core stores that command in the current callback's retained overlay frame instead of the TTL registry; the contribution is atomically replaced the next time that callback runs and remains visible across scheduler skips. Leave frame=false for intentionally persistent TTL commands. Unit commands default to bottom; screen commands default to screen. Supported alternative keys are w/h for width/height, background_color for bg_color, and num_points for segments. For lines, to_unit (or release-safe to_unit_handle) creates a unit-to-unit line. Both endpoints must resolve to current, on-screen Core units; otherwise the draw request fails closed. screen anchors are not valid for unit-to-unit lines.

items.text:
gos.overlay.draw_text("status", unit, {
  anchor = "top", x = 0, y = -24,
  text = "READY", color = "green", font_size = 16,
  shadow = true, center_x = true, ttl = 0.25,
})

gos.overlay.draw_line("line", {
  anchor = "screen", x1 = 100, y1 = 100, x2 = 220, y2 = 120,
  color = "cyan", thickness = 2,
})

-- Exact current unit-to-unit relationship. The same anchor is used at both
-- endpoints; x1/y1 offset the source and x2/y2 offset the destination.
gos.overlay.draw_line("cast_target", source, {
  to_unit = target, anchor = "center",
  color = "red", thickness = 2.5, frame = true,
})

gos.overlay.draw_rect("rect", unit, {
  anchor = "top", x = -40, y = -14, width = 80, height = 10,
  color = "yellow", filled = false, rounding = 2,
})

gos.overlay.draw_bar("health", unit, {
  anchor = "top", x = -45, y = -18, width = 90, height = 6,
  value = 0.5, color = "green",
  bg_color = { r = 12, g = 14, b = 16, a = 220 },
  border = true, border_color = "black",
})

gos.overlay.draw_circle("screen_circle", unit, {
  anchor = "center", radius = 18, color = "orange",
  segments = 32, filled = false,
})

gos.overlay.draw_image("icon", unit, {
  anchor = "top", path = SPRITE_PATH .. "icon.png",
  x = 0, y = -42, width = 24, height = 24,
  tint = "white", center_x = true,
})

gos.overlay.draw_rectangle is an alias for gos.overlay.draw_rect. Text supports font_size and shadow. Rectangles support filled, fill_color, rounding, and optional border fields. Bars clamp value to 0..1. Images use their texture size when width or height is omitted.

World-space circles must be unfilled and use game-world coordinate units. They may be anchored either to a current unit or to an explicit captured world position. A position-backed circle is independent of later unit visibility, so a persistent TTL marker remains at the supplied coordinates after that unit leaves the current snapshot. One coordinate unit currently represents 10 metres, so a 30-metre circle uses radius = 3:

gos.overlay.draw_circle("range", unit, {
  world_space = true,
  radius = 30 / 10,
  color = "cyan",
  segments = 64,
  thickness = 2,
})

-- Persistent last-known world position; no unit is required after submission.
gos.overlay.draw_circle("last_seen", {
  world_space = true,
  position = { x = last.x, y = last.y, z = last.z },
  radius = 8 / 10,
  color = "magenta",
  thickness = 3,
  ttl = 8,
})

The Release snapshot retains at most 512 active draw commands across frame-local and persistent output. A single callback may contribute at most 192 frame-local commands. IDs contain at most 31 bytes, text at most 63 bytes, and image paths at most 259 bytes. Oversized drawing IDs, text and image paths are truncated, not rejected; keep them within those byte limits to avoid collisions or unusable paths. Replacement matches callback owner, target identity, draw kind and the resulting ID. Reusing only the ID with another target or draw kind can leave a separate TTL drawing alive. Frame-local output supports at most 32 callback owners; these limits are shared with other scripts.

items.text:
API version: 1.0.0

Refresh a screen interaction rectangle and read mouse interaction state.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.overlay.interact(id, rect)

items.title: Contract and usage
items.text:
Overlay submissions are temporary. Refresh them from gos.on_tick before their TTL expires. Every draw function returns boolean success.

Unit-anchored commands accept either form:

gos.overlay.draw_text("id", unit, { ... })
gos.overlay.draw_text("id", { unit = unit, ... })
gos.overlay.draw_text("id", { unit_handle = "unit:...", ... })

Screen-space commands omit a unit and use anchor = "screen".

items.title: gos.overlay.interact(id, rect)
items.text:
Requires an active script callback. An empty or over-31-byte ID, invalid rectangle, nonpositive TTL, or wrong arguments raise a Lua error. Unlike ordinary draw IDs, interaction IDs are validated rather than truncated. Registers a temporary screen rectangle and returns left-mouse interaction:

local state = gos.overlay.interact("button", {
  x = 20, y = 20, width = 120, height = 28, ttl = 0.25,
})

-- state:
{
  hovered = boolean,
  pressed = boolean,
  down = boolean,
  released = boolean,
  clicked = boolean,
  mouse_x = number,
  mouse_y = number
}

Refresh the rectangle before its TTL expires. A press retains capture through release. The Release snapshot retains at most 64 active interaction rectangles, with at most 40 contributed by one callback owner, subject to the 32-owner frame ceiling. If registration or input observation is unavailable, the result can contain all false flags and zero coordinates with no separate availability flag. That state alone is not proof that the pointer is outside the rectangle; stay within the published budgets.

items.text:
API version: 1.0.0

Read current settings, enabled/active state and field values.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.settings.get(script_id)

items.title: Contract and usage
items.text: gos.settings.register and gos.settings.get raise Lua errors for invalid schemas, unknown registrations or unavailable required context. They do not return an empty settings snapshot on failure. gos.settings.set instead reports an accepted update with true, nil or a rejected update with false, error.

items.title: gos.settings.get(script_id)
items.text:
Returns the current snapshot:

{
  script_id = string,
  title = string,
  version = integer,
  enabled = boolean,
  active = boolean,
  primary = boolean,
  activation = {
    mode = "always" | "hold" | "toggle" | "manual",
    label = string,
    key = string
  },
  fields = { [field_key] = value },
  [field_key] = value
}

Field values are available both directly and through fields. active is computed by Core from enablement and activation mode. Use it as the execution gate:

gos.on_tick(function()
  Settings = gos.settings.get(SCRIPT_ID)
  if not Settings.enabled or not Settings.active then
    return
  end
end)

items.title: gos.settings.register
items.text:
API version: 1.0.0

Register this script's settings schema at load time, never from a tick.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.settings.register(script_id, schema)

items.title: Contract and usage
items.text: gos.settings.register and gos.settings.get raise Lua errors for invalid schemas, unknown registrations or unavailable required context. They do not return an empty settings snapshot on failure. gos.settings.set instead reports an accepted update with true, nil or a rejected update with false, error.

items.title: gos.settings.register(script_id, schema)
items.text:
Registers a settings schema while the script loads and returns its current settings snapshot. Calling it from a tick callback raises an error.

local SCRIPT_ID = "example_rotation"

local Settings = gos.settings.register(SCRIPT_ID, {
  title = "Example Rotation",
  version = 1,
  activation = {
    mode = "hold",       -- always, hold, toggle, or manual
    label = "Rotation Key",
    default = "mouse4",
  },
  fields = {
    {
      key = "show_status",
      type = "bool",
      label = "Show status",
      tooltip = "Draw the current rotation state.",
      default = true,
    },
    {
      key = "hp_threshold",
      type = "int",
      label = "HP threshold",
      default = 50,
      min = 1,
      max = 100,
      step = 1,
    },
    {
      key = "mode",
      type = "select",
      label = "Mode",
      default = "Single target",
      options = { "Single target", "Area" },
    },
    {
      key = "accent",
      type = "color",
      label = "Accent",
      default = "#00CCFFFF",
    },
  },
})

Supported field types:

Type Lua value Relevant schema keys bool boolean default number number default, min, max, step int integer default, min, max, step string string default, max_length (maximum 256) select string default, options (1-32 strings) hotkey string default color string default as #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA

Every field requires key, type, label, and default. Optional tooltip text appears in the settings UI. A schema can contain at most 256 fields. activation.default applies only to hold and toggle modes. While enabled, always and manual are active continuously, hold follows the configured key, and toggle changes state on a press.

Hotkey fields and hold/toggle activation keys use an inline capture button: click it, then press a keyboard key or mouse button. Escape cancels capture, and left/right mouse buttons are ignored. Uncommon keys persist as vk:0xNN; the UI displays their current keyboard-layout name. Optional activation keys also expose a separate clear button.

Fields may also declare UI visibility gates:

{
  key = "telekinetics_option",
  type = "bool",
  label = "Telekinetics option",
  default = false,
  disciplines = { "Telekinetics" },
  requires_ability = "Telekinetic Gust",
}

disciplines matches exact display discipline names and requires_ability matches a key in gos.abilities.loadout().known. Both gates must match when both are present. These gates affect settings visibility only; scripts must still validate their active loadout before using the setting.

Core shows gated rows while loadout identity is still pending or unavailable, then hides nonmatching rows once the loadout is ready. Validated values and activation keys persist across reloads.

items.title: Contract and usage

items.text:
API version: 1.0.0

Request an intentional persistent selected-target change; confirm it in a later snapshot.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.target.select(unit)

items.title: gos.target.select(unit)
items.text:
Requests a persistent change to the selected target. The argument must be a current-generation non-object GosUnit.

local ok, error = gos.target.select(ally)

true, nil means the request was queued or the unit was already selected. It does not claim that SWTOR applied the request; confirm a later gos.world().current_target or unit:is_current_target() snapshot. Operational failures return false with busy, invalid_target, stale_world, or unavailable. Invalid argument types and stale GosUnit userdata instead raise Lua errors; stale userdata raises stale_unit before a selection request is submitted. The request is manual target intent and remains selected. It is deliberately separate from explicit ability targeting: default explicit casts never call this API or mutate the player's selected target.

API version: 1.0.0

Acquire the current generation-bound world and its optional player and target.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.world()

items.title: gos.world()
items.text:
Returns the current generation-bound world:

{
  generation = integer,
  actor_epoch = "actors:..." | nil,
  actor_revision = integer | nil,
  player = GosUnit | nil,
  current_target = GosUnit | nil,
  units = function,
  resolve = function
}

player is the local player. current_target is the currently captured target. Either may be nil when unavailable. actor_epoch is the stable metadata-session token, not the per-tick generation. actor_revision changes when retained actor name metadata changes; ordinary unit movement does not change it. Both metadata fields are omitted when the actor-name authority is unavailable.

items.title: Unit Identity And Lifetime
items.text:
unit:name() reads the prepared current-unit view of the same actor-name authority used by combat-event actor labels and gos.actor_names. It does not perform a name lookup on demand. Its snapshot can be older than a later metadata read, but does not introduce a second name resolver.

Every GosUnit state-reading method raises stale_unit after its world generation expires. unit:handle() is the exception and remains available so the unit can be reacquired with a fresh world:resolve(handle).

Within one world, repeated lookups of the same unit compare equal with ==. Values from different generations compare unequal even when their handles match.

items.title: File Helpers
items.text:
Global helpers and their gos.file aliases:

Global Alias FileExist(path) gos.file.exists(path) ReadFile(path) gos.file.read(path) WriteFile(text, path, mode?) gos.file.write(text, path, mode?) DeleteFile(path) gos.file.delete(path) MakeDirectory(path) gos.file.mkdir(path) ListFiles(path, extension_filter?) gos.file.list(path, extension_filter?) DownloadFileAsync(url, path, callback?) gos.file.download_async(...) GetFromWebOrLocal(path, url, callback?) gos.file.get_from_web_or_local(...) UnzipArchive(path, target) gos.file.unzip(path, target)

FileExist returns whether the path is a regular file; ordinary absence returns false without an error. A rejected path returns false, error. ReadFile returns the binary-safe file contents, or nil, error. ListFiles returns an array of filenames, or nil, error; it does not recurse or promise sorted order.

Write/download/extraction helpers return true on success or false, error. DeleteFile returns false without an error when nothing was removed. MakeDirectory returns false without an error when the directory already existed; that is not a creation failure. An omitted second return value becomes nil in a two-variable assignment. WriteFile modes are w, wb, a, and ab; the default is w. Missing parent directories are created for a valid write path.

local path = CACHE_PATH .. "state.txt"
local ok, error = WriteFile("ready", path, "w")
if ok then
  local text = ReadFile(path)
end

ListFiles optionally filters by an exact extension such as .lua. It returns a partial list plus a warning only if its 16,384-entry safety ceiling is reached.

Despite its name, DownloadFileAsync performs blocking work in the current implementation. It is rejected in tick callbacks and should run only during loading. Its optional callback takes no arguments and runs before the helper returns, only after a successful download. Callback failure returns false, error even though the file may already have been written; failure does not imply rollback.

GetFromWebOrLocal ensures a file exists; it returns a boolean, not file contents. If a regular file already exists it invokes the same optional zero-argument callback without downloading. Only its download branch is rejected in a tick, but keep this potentially blocking helper at load time. The url argument is required and validated only on a cache miss; provide a valid URL whenever that branch is possible. An existing local file is not checked against a remote version or refreshed automatically. Callback failure also leaves an existing or newly downloaded file intact. Read the contents separately with ReadFile.

ZIP extraction is rejected in tick callbacks for the same blocking-work reason. Downloads accept HTTP or HTTPS and are limited to 256 MiB. ZIP extraction accepts .zip, validates archive paths, and limits total extracted size to 512 MiB.

DeleteFile(path) gos.file.delete(path) MakeDirectory(path) gos.file.mkdir(path) ListFiles(path, extension_filter?) gos.file.list(path, extension_filter?) DownloadFileAsync(url, path, callback?) gos.file.download_async(...) GetFromWebOrLocal(path, url, callback?) gos.file.get_from_web_or_local(...) UnzipArchive(path, target) gos.file.unzip(path, target)

FileExist returns whether the path is a regular file; ordinary absence returns false without an error. A rejected path returns false, error. ReadFile returns the binary-safe file contents, or nil, error. ListFiles returns an array of filenames, or nil, error; it does not recurse or promise sorted order.

Write/download/extraction helpers return true on success or false, error. DeleteFile returns false without an error when nothing was removed. MakeDirectory returns false without an error when the directory already existed; that is not a creation failure. An omitted second return value becomes nil in a two-variable assignment. local path = CACHE_PATH .. "state.txt"

  local text = ReadFile(path)
end

ListFiles optionally filters by an exact extension such as .lua. It returns a partial list plus a warning only if its 16,384-entry safety ceiling is reached.

Despite its name, DownloadFileAsync performs blocking work in the current implementation. It is rejected in tick callbacks and should run only during loading. Its optional callback takes no arguments and runs before the helper returns, only after a successful download. Callback failure returns false, error even though the file may already have been written; failure does not imply rollback.

GetFromWebOrLocal ensures a file exists; it returns a boolean, not file contents. If a regular file already exists it invokes the same optional zero-argument callback without downloading. Only its download branch is rejected in a tick, but keep this potentially blocking helper at load time. The url argument is required and validated only on a cache miss; provide a valid URL whenever that branch is possible. An existing local file is not checked against a remote version or refreshed automatically. Callback failure also leaves an existing or newly downloaded file intact. Read the contents separately with ReadFile.

ZIP extraction is rejected in tick callbacks for the same blocking-work reason. Downloads accept HTTP or HTTPS and are limited to 256 MiB. ZIP extraction accepts .zip, validates archive paths, and limits total extracted size to 512 MiB.

Structured logging uses a nonempty text value preferentially; otherwise a string message field must be supplied. These are input-field aliases, not two messages emitted together. Keep the final message meaningful and nonempty.

Structured logging:

local ok, error = gos.log.write({
  level = "info",     -- debug, info, success, warn, or error
  tag = "APL",
  text = "Queued Telekinetic Throw", -- message is an alias
  color = "cyan",
})

In the structured level field, "ok" is an alias for "success" and "warning" is an alias for "warn". These are level strings, not additional gos.log.ok or gos.log.warning functions. gos.log.write returns true, nil or false, error. The optional tag is limited to 24 bytes. Messages are sanitized and limited to 1024 bytes; multibyte text can reach that limit in fewer characters. Each script has its own bounded log buffer.

items.title: unit:effect
items.text:
API version: 1.0.0

Query a named or definition-key-matched aggregate; check readiness and completeness.

items.title: Signature
items.text: unit:effect(name, options)

items.title: Contract and usage
items.text:
Resolve the unit in the current world before querying it. A stale unit raises a Lua stale_unit error; this is distinct from a current unit returning a pending or unavailable effect observation. and status

Effect queries return the latest completed observation for that unit. They are snapshots, not synchronous reads.

status == "ready" means the latest valid completed poll, not a synchronous read at the time of the Lua call. Routine queued refreshes and combat effect notifications do not revoke that sample. Notifications only prioritize the next poll, so applications/removals become visible at the next publication. Timers age from their original sample anchor between polls.

Always check status and completeness: a complete ready observation proves presence/absence as of that poll. First capture, invalid owners/worlds, and actual acquisition failures remain distinguishable from an empty list. A missing execution opportunity is a scheduling wait, not an acquisition failure.

items.title: unit:effect(name, options?)
items.text:
Returns one case-insensitive named aggregate:

{
  status = "ready" | "pending" | "unavailable",
  reason = string,
  age_ms = integer | nil,
  truncated = boolean,

  -- Present only when status == "ready":
  present = boolean | nil,
  has_charges = boolean | nil,
  charge_conflicted = boolean | nil,
  stacks = integer | nil,
  has_timer = boolean | nil,
  remaining = number | nil,
  kind = "buff" | "debuff" | "passive" | "other" | "none" | nil,
  has_ownership = boolean | nil,
  mine = boolean | nil
}

Options:

local proc = player:effect("Tidal Force", {
  kind = "buff",       -- any, buff, debuff, passive, or other
  timed = true,         -- require or reject a timer
  charged = false,      -- require or reject a charge observation
})

if proc.status == "ready" and proc.present then
  local remaining = proc.has_timer and proc.remaining or nil
end

The singular query prefers exact local-player-owned rows when local and foreign effects share a name. mine is output metadata, not a filter. A truncated scan that cannot prove absence returns an unavailable result rather than present=false.

has_ownership=false means source identity is unavailable; mine=false alone does not establish foreign ownership. Kind follows the observed effect classification; an absent timer or an Other list does not prove an effect is passive.

Common public reasons are none, observation_pending, unsupported_unit, observation_capacity, and not_captured. Treat other reasons as diagnostics: log them and keep the observation unavailable instead of branching on them.

items.title: Exact effect identity
items.text:
definition_key identifies an effect definition, not an effect instance, a unit, or a castable ability. Same-name variants can have different keys. Treat keys as opaque and use an observed value; do not manufacture one. A key never makes a pending or historical row current. Both query forms accept a definition_key filter. To query only by key, pass an empty name to unit:effect("", { definition_key = observed_key }).

Plural rows expose has_duration and, when available, total duration in seconds. Duration is independent of remaining; do not estimate it from the first timer value you happen to see.

{
  status = "ready" | "pending" | "unavailable",
  reason = string,
  age_ms = integer | nil,
  last_known_age_ms = integer | nil,
  truncated = boolean,
  last_known_truncated = boolean,
  items = {
    {
      definition_key = "effectdef:<16 uppercase hex digits>" | nil,
      name = string,
      name_source = "client" | "core",
      freshness = "current",
      has_charges = boolean,
      charge_conflicted = boolean,
      stacks = integer | nil,
      has_timer = boolean,
      remaining = number | nil,
      has_duration = boolean,
      duration = number | nil,
      kind = "buff" | "debuff" | "passive" | "other",
      has_ownership = boolean,
      mine = boolean
    }
  },
  last_known_items = {
    {
      definition_key = "effectdef:<16 uppercase hex digits>" | nil,
      name = string,
      name_source = "client" | "core",
      freshness = "last_known",
      has_charges = boolean,
      charge_conflicted = boolean,
      stacks = integer | nil,
      has_timer = boolean,
      remaining = number | nil,
      has_duration = boolean,
      duration = number | nil,
      kind = "buff" | "debuff" | "passive" | "other",
      has_ownership = boolean,
      mine = boolean
    }
  }
}

The optional filter accepts name, kind, definition_key, timed, and charged with the same semantics as the singular query. A ready empty items table proves no matching current captured effect only when truncated == false. Pending, unavailable, or truncated observations do not prove absence.

items is always an array. It may be populated while an observation is pending/unavailable or while current enrichment is incomplete. Its timers are aged from their authoritative sample and removed at zero; those rows never make the observation ready and must not drive rotations, targeting, or tactical action cues. Unavailable observations remain unavailable for every unit; do not guess missing state.

local debuffs = target:effects({ kind = "debuff", timed = true })
if debuffs.status == "ready" then
  for _, effect in ipairs(debuffs.items) do
    if effect.mine then
      gos.log.debug(effect.name, effect.remaining or "untimed")
    end
  end
end

items.title: File Helpers
items.text:
Global helpers and their gos.file aliases:

Global Alias FileExist(path) gos.file.exists(path) ReadFile(path) gos.file.read(path) WriteFile(text, path, mode?) gos.file.write(text, path, mode?) DeleteFile(path) gos.file.delete(path) MakeDirectory(path) gos.file.mkdir(path) ListFiles(path, extension_filter?) gos.file.list(path, extension_filter?) DownloadFileAsync(url, path, callback?) gos.file.download_async(...) GetFromWebOrLocal(path, url, callback?) gos.file.get_from_web_or_local(...) UnzipArchive(path, target) gos.file.unzip(path, target)

FileExist returns whether the path is a regular file; ordinary absence returns false without an error. A rejected path returns false, error. ReadFile returns the binary-safe file contents, or nil, error. ListFiles returns an array of filenames, or nil, error; it does not recurse or promise sorted order.

Write/download/extraction helpers return true on success or false, error. DeleteFile returns false without an error when nothing was removed. MakeDirectory returns false without an error when the directory already existed; that is not a creation failure. An omitted second return value becomes nil in a two-variable assignment. WriteFile modes are w, wb, a, and ab; the default is w. Missing parent directories are created for a valid write path.

local path = CACHE_PATH .. "state.txt"
local ok, error = WriteFile("ready", path, "w")
if ok then
  local text = ReadFile(path)
end

ListFiles optionally filters by an exact extension such as .lua. It returns a partial list plus a warning only if its 16,384-entry safety ceiling is reached.

Despite its name, DownloadFileAsync performs blocking work in the current implementation. It is rejected in tick callbacks and should run only during loading. Its optional callback takes no arguments and runs before the helper returns, only after a successful download. Callback failure returns false, error even though the file may already have been written; failure does not imply rollback.

GetFromWebOrLocal ensures a file exists; it returns a boolean, not file contents. If a regular file already exists it invokes the same optional zero-argument callback without downloading. Only its download branch is rejected in a tick, but keep this potentially blocking helper at load time. The url argument is required and validated only on a cache miss; provide a valid URL whenever that branch is possible. An existing local file is not checked against a remote version or refreshed automatically. Callback failure also leaves an existing or newly downloaded file intact. Read the contents separately with ReadFile.

ZIP extraction is rejected in tick callbacks for the same blocking-work reason. Downloads accept HTTP or HTTPS and are limited to 256 MiB. ZIP extraction accepts .zip, validates archive paths, and limits total extracted size to 512 MiB.

items.title: world:resolve(handle)
items.text:
Resolves a well-formed opaque unit handle in the current generation. It returns a current GosUnit or nil when that identity is not currently captured.

local saved_handle, saved_epoch

gos.on_tick(function()
  local world = gos.world()
  if saved_epoch ~= world.actor_epoch then saved_handle = nil end
  saved_epoch = world.actor_epoch
  if world.current_target and saved_epoch then
    saved_handle = world.current_target:handle()
  end

  local current = saved_handle and world:resolve(saved_handle) or nil
end)

items.text:
A plain Lua ring buffer, independent of any GoS API. Save as bounded_history.lua in the shared module root and use require("bounded_history") from a script. Store copied records or handles, not generation-bound units. Do not mutate the buffer inside its each callback. This is a module, not an entry-point script to enable.

items.title: Complete code
items.text:
local History = {}
History.__index = History
function History.new(capacity)
  assert(type(capacity) == "number" and capacity % 1 == 0
      and capacity >= 1 and capacity <= 4096, "capacity must be 1..4096")
  return setmetatable({ capacity = capacity, count = 0, next = 1, rows = {} }, History)
end
function History:push(value)
  assert(value ~= nil, "history value cannot be nil")
  self.rows[self.next] = value
  self.next = self.next % self.capacity + 1
  self.count = math.min(self.count + 1, self.capacity)
end
function History:each(callback)
  local start = self.count == self.capacity and self.next or 1
  for offset = 0, self.count - 1 do
    callback(self.rows[(start + offset - 1) % self.capacity + 1])
  end
end
return History

items.title: Bounded incoming damage counter
items.text:
Counts observed raw damage targeting the local player after subscription, not effective damage or a full fight history. Resets when disabled, when the player disappears, or when identity changes. A nonzero lost count means the total is incomplete. Work is capped at four batches (256 events) per callback; there is no per-hit logging or stored history.

View or save the Lua source

items.title: Complete code
items.text:
local ID = "example_incoming_damage"
gos.settings.register(ID, {
  title = "Example: Incoming Damage", version = 1,
  activation = { mode = "always" }, fields = {},
})
local cursor, owner
local total, samples, dropped = 0, 0, 0
local MAX_BATCHES = 4

gos.on_tick(function()
  local settings = gos.settings.get(ID)
  local player = gos.world().player
  local handle = player and player:handle() or nil
  if not settings.enabled or not settings.active or not handle then
    cursor, owner = nil, nil
    total, samples, dropped = 0, 0, 0
    return
  end
  if handle ~= owner then
    owner, cursor = handle, nil
    total, samples, dropped = 0, 0, 0
  end
  for _ = 1, MAX_BATCHES do
    local batch = gos.events.combat(cursor)
    cursor = batch.cursor
    dropped = dropped + batch.dropped
    for _, event in ipairs(batch.events) do
      if event.kind == "damage" and event.target_handle == handle
          and type(event.amount) == "number" then
        total = total + event.amount
        samples = samples + 1
      end
    end
    if not batch.more then break end
  end
  gos.overlay.draw_text("example_damage", {
    anchor = "screen", x = 30, y = 110, frame = true,
    text = string.format("Taken %.0f | hits %d | lost %d", total, samples, dropped),
    color = dropped > 0 and "orange" or "white", font_size = 16,
  })
end, { interval_ms = 100 })

items.title: Commando: persistent position markers
items.text:
Live-script excerpt - from commando_stealth_detector.lua, used by the project's live-tested scripts. The functions below are copied unchanged.

The Commando stealth detector draws two circles at a captured position. Expiry belongs to the recorded observation, so redrawing does not give an old marker a fresh lifetime. The same pattern works for encounter notes, last-seen locations and timed world annotations.

View or save the excerpt

Integration fragment, not a standalone rotation

This method belongs to the detector object. It requires self.markers, the module's finite and valid_position helpers, and an options table. Each marker contains position, expiresAt in monotonic seconds, and eventName. Keep the marker collection bounded in the producer; do not enable this excerpt by itself.

items.title: Code from the live script
items.text:
function Detector:draw_markers(now, options)
    now = finite(now) and now or 0.0
    for serial, marker in pairs(self.markers) do
        if type(marker) ~= "table" or not finite(marker.expiresAt) or marker.expiresAt <= now then
            self.markers[serial] = nil
        elseif type(options) == "table" and options.enabled ~= false and
            gos.overlay and type(gos.overlay.draw_circle) == "function" and
            valid_position(marker.position) then
            local remaining = math.max(0.05, marker.expiresAt - now)
            local color = marker.eventName == "Force Camouflage" and "orange" or "magenta"
            pcall(gos.overlay.draw_circle, "stl_o_" .. tostring(serial), {
                world_space = true, position = marker.position, radius = 0.8,
                color = color, segments = 48, thickness = 3, ttl = remaining,
            })
            pcall(gos.overlay.draw_circle, "stl_i_" .. tostring(serial), {
                world_space = true, position = marker.position, radius = 0.18,
                color = color, segments = 24, thickness = 2.5, ttl = remaining,
            })
        end
    end
end

items.title: How to use the pattern
items.text:
A top-level owner supplies now = gos.time_ms() / 1000. The observer records positions before units disappear; this draw method uses those copied coordinates rather than retaining a GosUnit.

Call detector:draw_markers(now, { enabled = true }) on the existing detector instance. Use the same clock for creation and expiry. Stable IDs replace previous drawings. Passing enabled = false stops refreshes; an already submitted TTL drawing can remain until its previously supplied TTL expires.

radius = 0.8 is eight metres at the current world scale. The outer and inner circles make a single position easy to see. Orange distinguishes the source script's Force Camouflage marker; magenta is its other marker color. This is a last-observed position, not proof of where a hidden player is now.

items.title: Operative: maintain Kolto Probe stacks
items.text:
Live-script excerpt - from operative_medicine.lua, used by the project's live-tested scripts. The functions below are copied unchanged.

This is the Medicine route's actual Kolto Probe refresh decision: first build the configured stack count, then refresh an expiring HoT, and never interpret an unavailable observation as a missing HoT.

View or save the excerpt

Integration fragment, not a standalone rotation

This function runs inside the Medicine module. It requires mine_effect_snapshot, finite_number, KOLTO_PROBE, KOLTO_PROBE_MAX_STACKS, and a policy with koltoProbeRefreshSeconds. The snapshot helper returns nil when unresolved or a table with stacks and optional remaining in seconds. This decision fragment does not cast or own a command.

items.title: Code from the live script
items.text:
local function kolto_probe_needs_refresh(unit, policy)
    local state = mine_effect_snapshot(unit, KOLTO_PROBE, "buff")
    -- Unknown observation is not evidence that the HoT is missing; fail closed
    -- so the route cannot spam Kolto Probe while Core catches up.
    if state == nil then return false, "observation_unknown" end
    if state.stacks < KOLTO_PROBE_MAX_STACKS then
        return true, "build_" .. tostring(state.stacks + 1)
    end
    if finite_number(state.remaining) and
        state.remaining <= policy.koltoProbeRefreshSeconds then
        return true, "refresh_expiring"
    end
    return false, "healthy"
end

items.title: How to use the pattern
items.text:
The first return is whether to nominate Kolto Probe. The second explains the decision: observation_unknown, build_1, build_2, refresh_expiring, or healthy. These strings are decisions from this helper, not global ability result codes.

Evaluate it for a freshly resolved eligible ally. The dispatcher still owns target selection, learned-ability checks, energy, emergency priorities and the shared executor. Do not submit a new command repeatedly just because this function returns true.

When porting the helper, preserve unavailable state, ownership and incomplete-charge distinctions from the effect API. In particular, mine = false without has_ownership = true is not proof that a HoT belongs to someone else. A missing timer is not zero seconds. The refresh threshold comes from policy; this excerpt does not prescribe one universal PvE/PvP value.

items.title: Current helper assumptions
items.text: The surrounding mine_effect_snapshot helper is not included in this excerpt. In the current source it treats a ready row with mine ~= true as zero owned stacks, and uses one stack when a present owned effect has no usable charge count. Those are source-module assumptions, not guarantees of the public effect API. For a reusable implementation, require has_ownership before treating a row as foreign and preserve unknown charge counts rather than copying those assumptions into a generic HoT tracker. The observation_unknown branch only covers a snapshot helper that actually returns nil.

The useful pattern is to predict when an observation should arrive without pretending it has already arrived. The route learns Throw tick timing, counts actual damage events against its starting stack observation, and keeps that expectation separate from the buff stacks that authorize normal spender selection.

Integration fragment, not a standalone rotation

items.title: Three different kinds of evidence
items.text:
Evidence What the live code does What it does not prove Predicted next tick time Learns activation-to-first-tick and tick-to-tick timing; publishes presence_throw_predicted_next_tick_ms That damage occurred, or that a stack was granted Observed Throw damage ticks Adds actual matching events to the starting stack count; marks presence_stack_tick_ready when the total reaches four That the effect snapshot already contains four usable charges Observed PoM buff stacks presence_projection(state) returns ready only when the validated observed stack count is at least PRESENCE_MAX_STACKS That a subsequent command was accepted or activated

Time passing never increments the tick count. The helper increments it only for a matching damage event while the tracked Throw is active. Despite its name, the current presence_projection function returns observed stacks and the source label "observed"; it does not promote predicted stacks into readiness.

items.title: Follow one Throw
items.text:
An activation event starts a new channel lifecycle. The observer matches the local player's source handle and the current Throw activation handle. Damage ticks match that player, the resolved Throw name, an active lifecycle and a numeric timestamp. It does not count every damage event on the target.

The channel starts from presence_last_observed_stacks. Actual damage events advance presence_throw_tick_count; a known starting count plus those ticks reaching four creates an event-backed expectation. The full route reconciles the starting count with subsequent buff observations, rather than assuming every channel began at zero.

The timing estimator keeps running means, not an event history. After two ticks in the current channel, its interval estimate is (last_tick - first_tick) / (tick_count - 1). Before then, the code can use its explicitly retained historical interval mean. Without timing evidence, the next-tick estimate remains nil.

items.title: Reconcile before spending
items.text:
The surrounding tick function performs the reconciliation described here; it is not included in the six-function download. Keep this step when integrating the observer. It runs after the route has read a valid state, before normal action selection.

If event counting expects four stacks but the buff still shows fewer, normal selection waits with presence_stack_tick_wait_effect. To tell a delayed snapshot from contrary evidence, the route computes the effect sample time as state.now * 1000.0 - math.max(0.0, ageMs). A sample at least 2 ms newer than the threshold damage event, still showing fewer than four stacks, clears the candidate and marks it disproved for that lifecycle. The 2 ms margin comes from the source's integer-timestamp rounding guard; it is not a general network-latency timeout.

A missing sample age cannot establish that ordering. It must not be replaced with zero. Likewise, observed_presence_stacks is safe here because the route has already rejected unavailable effect observations and present buffs with unknown charge counts. Do not call it directly on an unvalidated API response: its zero return is not an unknown-data policy.

The following is an illustrative trace, not a recorded fight. Assume two starting stacks, one received tick, and a predicted next tick at 1700 ms. The last two rows show different possible fresh observations.

Observation Interpretation Clock reaches 1700 ms; no new damage event No new tick or stack is invented Matching damage arrives at 1700 ms; buff still says three Two starting stacks plus two received ticks predicts completion; wait for the buff The three-stack snapshot was sampled at 1699 ms It predates the damage event and cannot disprove the candidate A three-stack snapshot was sampled at 1702 ms Fresh contrary evidence clears the event-backed candidate A validated snapshot instead reports four stacks Normal selection can nominate an eligible spender; the executor still owns submission and confirmation

items.title: Integration requirements
items.text:
Use PRESENCE_MAX_STACKS = 4, the source module's safe_method, emit_diagnostic and number_text, and the documented gos.abilities.info / gos.events.combat APIs. The effect adapter prepares state.effects.presenceOfMind with present, validated stacks, and optional ageMs mapped from public age_ms. state.now is in seconds; event timestamps and learned timing values are in milliseconds.

The closure state must be declared before the four indented helpers, inside the same route instance. These are the source initial values; do not turn them into shared globals:

items.title: Code from the live script
items.text:
The first four functions are the closure-local observer and its helpers. The last two show the observed-stack readiness boundary. Their original indentation is preserved to make the different scopes visible.

    local function update_running_mean(mean, samples, value)
        if type(value) ~= "number" or value <= 0.0 then
            return mean, samples
        end
        samples = samples + 1
        if type(mean) ~= "number" then
            return value, samples
        end
        return mean + (value - mean) / samples, samples
    end

    local function reset_presence_lifecycle(reset_cursor)
        presence_throw_active = false
        presence_throw_tick_count = 0
        presence_stack_tick_ready = false
        presence_stack_tick_ready_ms = nil
        presence_stack_tick_disproved = false
        presence_throw_start_stacks = nil
        presence_throw_activation_ms = nil
        presence_throw_first_tick_ms = nil
        presence_throw_last_tick_ms = nil
        presence_throw_predicted_next_tick_ms = nil
        presence_completion_observed = false
        presence_event_fault = nil
        if reset_cursor then
            presence_stack_tick_suppressed = false
            presence_combat_cursor = nil
            presence_player_handle = nil
            presence_throw_handle = nil
            presence_last_observed_stacks = nil
        end
    end

    local function report_presence_event_fault(options, reason)
        if type(options) ~= "table" or options.decisionLog ~= true then
            presence_event_fault = nil
            return
        end
        if presence_event_fault == reason then
            return
        end
        presence_event_fault = reason
        emit_diagnostic(options, "warn",
            "route=balance phase=presence_lifecycle state=unavailable" ..
            " reason=" .. tostring(reason))
    end

    local function observe_presence_lifecycle(options, world)
        local player = world and world.player or nil
        local player_handle = safe_method(player, "handle")
        local throw_info = gos.abilities.info("Telekinetic Throw")
        local throw_handle = type(throw_info) == "table" and
            throw_info.activation_handle or nil
        local throw_name = type(throw_info) == "table" and
            type(throw_info.name) == "string" and throw_info.name or nil
        if type(player_handle) ~= "string" or
            type(throw_handle) ~= "string" or
            type(throw_name) ~= "string" then
            return false, false, nil, 0, 0
        end

        if (presence_player_handle ~= nil and
                presence_player_handle ~= player_handle) or
            (presence_throw_handle ~= nil and
                presence_throw_handle ~= throw_handle) then
            reset_presence_lifecycle(true)
            presence_first_tick_mean_ms = nil
            presence_first_tick_samples = 0
            presence_tick_interval_mean_ms = nil
            presence_tick_interval_samples = 0
        end
        presence_player_handle = player_handle
        presence_throw_handle = throw_handle

        local batch = gos.events.combat(presence_combat_cursor)
        if type(batch) ~= "table" or type(batch.cursor) ~= "number" or
            type(batch.dropped) ~= "number" or
            type(batch.more) ~= "boolean" or
            type(batch.events) ~= "table" then
            reset_presence_lifecycle(false)
            report_presence_event_fault(options, "invalid_batch")
            return false, false, nil, 0, 0
        end

        presence_combat_cursor = batch.cursor
        if batch.dropped > 0 then
            reset_presence_lifecycle(false)
            report_presence_event_fault(options,
                "dropped_" .. tostring(batch.dropped))
        else
            presence_event_fault = nil
        end

        for index = 1, #batch.events do
            local event = batch.events[index]
            if type(event) == "table" and
                event.source_handle == player_handle then
                local lifecycle_event = event.kind == "ability" and
                    event.ability_handle == throw_handle
                local damage_tick = event.kind == "damage" and
                    presence_throw_active and event.name == throw_name and
                    type(event.timestamp) == "number"
                if lifecycle_event and event.action == "ability_activate" then
                    presence_throw_active = true
                    presence_throw_tick_count = 0
                    presence_stack_tick_ready = false
                    presence_stack_tick_ready_ms = nil
                    presence_stack_tick_disproved = false
                    presence_stack_tick_suppressed = false
                    presence_throw_start_stacks = presence_last_observed_stacks
                    presence_throw_activation_ms =
                        type(event.timestamp) == "number" and event.timestamp or nil
                    presence_throw_first_tick_ms = nil
                    presence_throw_last_tick_ms = nil
                    presence_throw_predicted_next_tick_ms =
                        type(presence_throw_activation_ms) == "number" and
                        type(presence_first_tick_mean_ms) == "number" and
                        presence_throw_activation_ms + presence_first_tick_mean_ms or nil
                    presence_completion_observed = false
                elseif damage_tick then
                    local previous_tick_ms = presence_throw_last_tick_ms
                    presence_throw_tick_count = presence_throw_tick_count + 1
                    if not presence_stack_tick_ready and
                        not presence_stack_tick_disproved and
                        type(presence_throw_start_stacks) == "number" and
                        presence_throw_start_stacks + presence_throw_tick_count >=
                            PRESENCE_MAX_STACKS then
                        if presence_stack_tick_suppressed then
                            emit_diagnostic(options, "debug",
                                "route=balance phase=presence_handoff" ..
                                " state=late_stack_tick_ignored" ..
                                " reason=spender_executor_owned" ..
                                " start=" ..
                                    number_text(presence_throw_start_stacks, 0) ..
                                " ticks=" .. tostring(presence_throw_tick_count))
                        else
                            presence_stack_tick_ready = true
                            presence_stack_tick_ready_ms = event.timestamp
                            emit_diagnostic(options, "info",
                                "route=balance phase=presence_handoff" ..
                                " state=stack_tick_observed" ..
                                " start=" ..
                                    number_text(presence_throw_start_stacks, 0) ..
                                " ticks=" .. tostring(presence_throw_tick_count))
                        end
                    end
                    if presence_throw_first_tick_ms == nil then
                        presence_throw_first_tick_ms = event.timestamp
                        if type(presence_throw_activation_ms) == "number" and
                            event.timestamp > presence_throw_activation_ms then
                            presence_first_tick_mean_ms,
                                presence_first_tick_samples = update_running_mean(
                                    presence_first_tick_mean_ms,
                                    presence_first_tick_samples,
                                    event.timestamp - presence_throw_activation_ms)
                        end
                    end
                    if type(previous_tick_ms) == "number" and
                        event.timestamp > previous_tick_ms then
                        presence_tick_interval_mean_ms,
                            presence_tick_interval_samples = update_running_mean(
                                presence_tick_interval_mean_ms,
                                presence_tick_interval_samples,
                                event.timestamp - previous_tick_ms)
                    end
                    presence_throw_last_tick_ms = event.timestamp

                    local next_interval_ms = nil
                    if presence_throw_tick_count >= 2 and
                        type(presence_throw_first_tick_ms) == "number" and
                        event.timestamp > presence_throw_first_tick_ms then
                        next_interval_ms =
                            (event.timestamp - presence_throw_first_tick_ms) /
                            (presence_throw_tick_count - 1)
                    elseif type(presence_tick_interval_mean_ms) == "number" then
                        next_interval_ms = presence_tick_interval_mean_ms
                    end
                    presence_throw_predicted_next_tick_ms =
                        type(next_interval_ms) == "number" and
                        event.timestamp + next_interval_ms or nil
                elseif lifecycle_event and
                    (event.action == "ability_interrupt" or
                        event.action == "ability_cancel") then
                    reset_presence_lifecycle(false)
                elseif lifecycle_event and
                    event.action == "ability_deactivate" then
                    if presence_throw_active then
                        presence_completion_observed = true
                    end
                    presence_throw_active = false
                end
            end
        end

        return batch.more == true, batch.cursor, #batch.events, batch.dropped
    end

local function observed_presence_stacks(state)
    local presence = state.effects.presenceOfMind
    return presence.present and
        type(presence.stacks) == "number" and presence.stacks or 0
end

local function presence_projection(state)
    local observed = observed_presence_stacks(state)
    if observed >= PRESENCE_MAX_STACKS then
        return true, observed, "observed"
    end
    return false, observed, "observed"
end

items.title: Sage / Seer: deterministic healing triage
items.text:
Live-script excerpt - from sage_seer.lua, used by the project's live-tested scripts. The functions below are copied unchanged.

This pure-Lua comparator comes directly from the Seer route. It picks the lower health ratio, then the larger missing-health amount, then a stable handle order. It demonstrates useful module logic beyond calling API functions.

View or save the excerpt

Integration fragment, not a standalone rotation

Supply validated living-health values: 0 < current <= maximum, with a positive maximum. rhs is either nil or a candidate containing current, maximum, and handle. Handles must be comparable strings. This function ranks already eligible candidates; it does not validate range, line of sight, group policy or cast readiness.

items.title: Code from the live script
items.text:
local function friendlier(current, maximum, handle, rhs)
    if rhs == nil then
        return true
    end
    local lhs_ratio = current * rhs.maximum
    local rhs_ratio = rhs.current * maximum
    if lhs_ratio ~= rhs_ratio then
        return lhs_ratio < rhs_ratio
    end
    local lhs_missing = maximum - current
    local rhs_missing = rhs.maximum - rhs.current
    if lhs_missing ~= rhs_missing then
        return lhs_missing > rhs_missing
    end
    return handle < rhs.handle
end

items.title: How to use the pattern
items.text:
Comparing current * rhs.maximum against rhs.current * maximum avoids dividing by a maximum inside the comparison. Absolute missing health breaks a ratio tie; the opaque handle then makes the result deterministic instead of depending on iteration order. Comparing handles is allowed; parsing their contents is not.

For example, a 40/100 candidate beats a 90/100 candidate. At the same 50% ratio, 100/200 wins over 50/100 because it is missing more health.

Feed it eligible rows collected from one fresh world. Save only copied health values and handles across ticks, then resolve the selected handle again before acting. The full Seer route applies additional emergency, self-preservation and maintenance policy: this comparator is not the whole healing priority.

These are the Concentration route's real resource decisions. Zealous Strike needs room for its Focus gain. Zen checks its setting, a known Centering observation, stack count, resource room and an available follow-up spender before asking whether the ability is usable.

These functions use the route's prepared state and shared definitions: ZEALOUS_FOCUS_GAIN, ZEN_CENTERING_COST, ZEN_IMMEDIATE_FOCUS_GAIN, number_text, zen_has_spender, and can_use. State includes abilities, focus, focusMax and optional centering. Keep those dependencies with the functions when porting; the excerpt alone is not an entry point.

items.title: Code from the live script
items.text:
local function zealous_focus_has_room(state)
    return state.abilities["Zealous Strike"] ~= nil and
        state.focus <= state.focusMax - ZEALOUS_FOCUS_GAIN
end

local function zen_gate(state, options)
    if type(options) == "table" and options.automaticZen == false then
        return false, "setting_disabled"
    end
    if state.centering == nil then
        return false, "centering_unavailable"
    end
    if not state.centering.present then
        return false, "centering_absent"
    end
    if type(state.centering.stacks) ~= "number" then
        return false, "centering_stacks_unavailable"
    end
    if state.centering.stacks < ZEN_CENTERING_COST then
        return false, "centering_" .. number_text(state.centering.stacks, 0) ..
            "_of_" .. tostring(ZEN_CENTERING_COST)
    end
    local focus_room = state.focusMax - state.focus
    if focus_room < ZEN_IMMEDIATE_FOCUS_GAIN then
        return false, "focus_room_" .. number_text(focus_room, 0) ..
            "_need_" .. tostring(ZEN_IMMEDIATE_FOCUS_GAIN)
    end
    if not zen_has_spender(state, options) then
        return false, "no_spender_after_focus_gain"
    end
    local castable, reason = can_use(state, "Zen", options)
    if not castable then
        return false, reason
    end
    return true, "centering_30"
end

items.title: How to use the pattern
items.text:
The resource-room test is separate from ability readiness. A known ability can be ready while a generator would waste resource; conversely, resource room does not prove a cast will be accepted.

zen_gate preserves the difference between missing Centering data, an absent effect and a known effect with insufficient stacks. It returns a boolean plus a route-local explanation. The live route uses 30 Centering for this branch, but its constants and spender logic belong to that route's supported loadout; this is not a universal Sentinel or Marauder rotation.

After the gate succeeds, let the top-level executor submit and observe the command. Do not treat this decision, or a queued result, as activation proof. The pattern generalizes to proc spenders, energy recovery and burst preparation without inventing missing resource values.

items.title: One action, one command owner
items.text:
A hold-key example using the optional ability_executor helper. It attempts the configured known hostile-target ability while held, subject to current readiness. It is not a complete rotation. Set a learned hostile-target ability before enabling (the default is Force Stun). No selected-target fallback is enabled. The helper owns polling and cancellation.

View or save the Lua source

items.title: Complete code
items.text:
local AbilityExecutor = require("ability_executor")
local executor = AbilityExecutor.new()
local ID = "example_single_action"
gos.settings.register(ID, {
  title = "Example: Single Action", version = 1,
  activation = { mode = "hold", label = "Action key", default = "mouse4" },
  fields = {{ key = "ability", type = "string", label = "Ability name", default = "Force Stun", max_length = 96 }},
})
gos.on_tick(function()
  executor:tick() -- Poll even after the activation key is released.
  local settings = gos.settings.get(ID)
  if not settings.enabled or not settings.active then
    if executor:has_pending() then executor:cancel("inactive") end
    return
  end
  if executor:has_pending() then return end
  local loadout = gos.abilities.loadout()
  if loadout.status ~= "ready" or not loadout.known[settings.ability] then return end
  local world = gos.world()
  local target = world.current_target
  if not world.player or not target or target:reaction() ~= "hostile" then return end
  local hp = target:hp()
  if not hp or hp.current <= 0 then return end
  if not gos.abilities.can_cast(settings.ability, target).ok then return end
  executor:submit(settings.ability, target, {
    idempotencyKey = "example_action:" .. target:handle(),
    target_fallback = "none",
  })
end)

items.title: Three different questions
items.text:
Can it be attempted now? gos.abilities.can_cast reports a current local readiness result. Pending or unavailable checks do not own a command. wait_ms is observed timing, not a future scheduling promise.

Was it queued? gos.abilities.cast can accept a request for asynchronous processing. Keep the returned command handle; do not repeat the submission on every tick while it is owned.

Did it start? Inspect command status. terminal means the command reached a lifecycle boundary, not necessarily successful activation. acknowledged and activation_proven are start evidence. Terminal submitted does not itself prove a start; retained status may gain an outcome later. Unknown results stay unknown.

items.title: Readiness is not queue eligibility
items.text: can_cast() tests current readiness. Omitted-target cast() requests can have different queue admission while a GCD or channel is ending. Explicit units/handles use ready-now admission, even when currently selected. See target and readiness semantics before choosing a pre-cast gate.

items.title: Keep one owner
items.text:
For continuous behavior, use one ability executor at the top level. Pass it to sub-routes, poll it at the top level, and do not let independent modules cancel each other's work. Continue polling after an activation key is released so cancellation and cleanup are observed. A failed cancellation is not permission to forget the command.

The single-action example demonstrates that structure. It is deliberately not a complete class rotation.

items.title: Explicit targets are deliberate
items.text:
Pass a current unit or its opaque handle for an explicit target. An explicit cast does not persistently change the visible selected target by default. Use gos.target.select only for an intentional persistent selection change; confirm the later snapshot.

Selected-target fallback is opt-in. Leave target_fallback="none" when action identity matters. A failed target must not silently turn a heal, interrupt or other action into a cast on someone else.

items.title: Do not infer outcomes from timers
items.text: A GCD change, cooldown movement, or an empty current-cast field is not proof that a particular command succeeded or failed. Use the documented result fields. Avoid guessed timeouts that repeatedly recreate ownership. For exact shapes and result codes, read the ability reference.

items.title: Choose the stream, not a snapshot
items.text: gos.events.combat(cursor) is the ordered event stream. The initial call with no cursor subscribes at the current head; it does not replay a whole earlier fight. Keep the returned cursor for subsequent calls. The casts and instants helpers describe current presentation snapshots and are not a historical log.

items.title: Source and destination are different
items.text: For outgoing damage compare event.source_handle to the player's handle. For incoming damage compare event.target_handle. The optional combat_events module's player and target scopes match destinations. A unit may no longer resolve by the time you process an event; its captured identity is still useful for comparison, but its current health or position is unknown.

items.title: Retain actor labels with their epoch
items.text: Use optional source_name and target_name for captured display text. Keep each retained actor's actor_epoch with its handle; names are not grouping keys. For a later label, read gos.actor_names(handles, saved_epoch) in bounded update batches, including after the last combat hit. Preserve a delivered name when metadata is no longer retained. If the epoch changes, keep the old history's captured labels and stop enriching it from the new session. Resolving an event handle for current health or position also requires a matching actor epoch. See the actor metadata contract.

items.title: Bound processing and disclose gaps
items.text: Each stream call returns up to 64 events with more and dropped. Use a fixed pass budget and carry the cursor forward. Do not loop until the stream is empty without a cap. A dropped count means overwritten input, not zero damage. Show that a graph or total is incomplete.

items.title: Classify only supported evidence
items.text:
Do not call every effect a crowd-control event or every cast ending an interrupt. Inspect the published kind, optional action, and result. An interrupted or immune action is not a damage hit unless the actual event says damage and supplies an amount. Unrecognized classifications should remain visible as unknown, or be omitted with a documented rule, not guessed from ability-name substrings.

When a tool retains data, bound both record count and age. Cache metadata outside hot processing and show the distinction between current observations and last-known presentation. See the counter example and public event schema.

items.title: 1. Start read-only
items.text:
Open the status panel example and save its Lua source in the active scripts directory used by your GoS Lua manager. Add or reload the script there, enable it, then enable its Show panel setting. Use your installation's configured directory; a development-repository path is not required.

You should see a small health label. If the player or health snapshot is unavailable, the label says so. The script never casts or changes targets.

items.title: 2. Understand the three parts
items.text:
Settings are registered once when the script loads. A callback is registered with gos.on_tick. Each callback reads a fresh world, performs bounded work, and returns. A requested interval is a scheduling cadence, not an exact timer guarantee.

Use gos.settings.get inside the callback to read current enablement and values. Registration is load-time-only. Unhandled callback errors disable that callback until scripts are reloaded; check the script log rather than repeatedly re-enabling a broken script.

items.title: 3. Add one feature at a time
items.text: Try the incoming damage counter, then a position marker. Only after those are understood, examine command ownership and the single-action example.

items.title: Common mistakes
items.text:
A GosUnit belongs to one world generation. Store its handle when identity must survive a tick, then resolve it in a fresh world. Never keep an old unit object and call its methods later.

nil is unavailable, not zero. pending is not absent. A successful queue submission is not proof that an ability started. File and network operations do not belong in a tick callback.
